SODReasonCodes.Name: A_A1+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : The integrity of AA master data is the basis for the integrity of the AA transactional data based on this master data.
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : The integrity of AA master data is the basis for the integrity of all transactional data based on it. Therefore it is strongly recommended having a separate group maintaining the AA master data. Moreover, the combination of master data maintenance with transactional data may encourage fraudulent action by enabling the creating fictitious master data and performing fake transactions on these inappropriate master data.

SODReasonCodes.Name: A_A3+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : No user should have access to two consecutive stages within the AA flow.
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : No user should have access to two consecutive stages within the AA flow.

SODReasonCodes.Name: A_F1+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : The integrity of FI master data is the basis for the integrity of the FI transactional data based on this master data.
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : The integrity of FI master data is the basis for the integrity of the FI transactional data based on this master data. Therefore it is strongly recommended having a separate group maintaining the FI master data. Moreover, the combination of master data maintenance with transactional data may encourage fraudulent action by enabling the creating fictitious master data and performing fake transactions on these inappropriate master data. Examples: - An invalid or fictitious G/L account could be created, fraudulent postings could be performed to this account and could later be concealed by clearing the account. - A fake bank could be created and a payment / check could be generated for that bank in the payment run. - A user creates a fictitious vendor, creates a PO on the vendor, posts the goods receipt (and receives the goods), and posts the invoice for it. This completes the tree way match, which releases the invoice for payment. - A user should not be able to update the Vendor Master File, Post an Invoice, Process Payment Settlement and Post Outgoing Payments. - A user should not be able to maintaine Customer Master File, establish Credit Limits, create Sales Order and Process Credit Memos. - A user could unblock a customer in order to allow the processing of a sales without the consent of Finance.

SODReasonCodes.Name: A_F3+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : No user should have access to two consecutive stages within the FI flow.
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : No user should have access to two consecutive stages within the FI flow. Examples: - Unauthorized purchase orders could be created and/or released and payment for these orders could be triggered by entering fictitious vendor invoices or the purchase order could be concealed in the G/L by posting and clearing entries in the G/L. - Inadequate deliveries may be concealed by posting and/or clearing entries in the G/L. - A user should not be able to Post an Invoice, Process Payment Settlement and Post Outgoing Payments. - A user should not be able to input customer remittances and cover defalcation with a credit note.

SODReasonCodes.Name: A_F2+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : The payment functionality should be segregated from the other transactional data (postings, goods receipts, etc.).
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : The payment functionality should be segregated from the other transactional data (postings, goods receipts, etc.). Inappropriate or fraudulent vendor invoices could be entered and payments for these invoices could be generated through the automatic payment run and/or by creating or changing checks. Example: - Payments could be processed through the automatic payment run or by creating manual checks by entering inappropriate or fictitious purchase orders. Especially in combination with vendor master data maintenance access, these fictitious purchase orders could be created for fictitious vendors.

SODReasonCodes.Name: A_M1+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : The integrity of MM master data is the basis for the integrity of all transactional data based on it.
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : The integrity of MM master data is the basis for the integrity of all transactional data based on it. Therefore it is strongly recommended having a separate group maintaining the MM master data. Moreover, the combination of master data maintenance with transactional data may encourage fraudulent action by enabling the creating fictitious master data and performing fake transactions on these inappropriate master data.

SODReasonCodes.Name: A_M3+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : No user should have access to two consecutive stages within the MM flow.
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : No user should have access to two consecutive stages within the MM flow. Examples: - A user should not be able to create and approve Purchase Requisitions / Purchase Orders / Outline Agreements beyond a certain threshold to ensure all purchases are justified, are for business purposes, are from preferred vendors, etc. The release actions constitute a key controls in the purchasing process. - Inappropriate or fictitious purchase orders or stock transport orders could be created and/or purchase orders or stock transport orders could be modified to conceal inadequate delivery of goods or theft of parts of the deliveries. - A user creates a fictitious vendor, creates a PO on the vendor, posts the goods receipt (and receives the goods), and posts the invoice for it. This completes the tree way match, which releases the invoice for payment. - Posting Physical Inventory Adjustments should be segregated from Inputting actual Physical Inventory Count results. If not, inventory quantities could be adjusted to cover inventory defalcation.

SODReasonCodes.Name: A_P1+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : The integrity of HR master data is the basis for the integrity of the HR transactional data based on it.
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : The integrity of HR master data is the basis for the integrity of all transactional data based on it. Therefore it is strongly recommended having a separate group maintaining the HR master data. Moreover, the combination of master data maintenance with transactional data may encourage fraudulent action by enabling the creating fictitious master data and performing fake transactions on these inappropriate master data. Example: - Combined access to sarlary master data and the payroll run, may encourage fraudulent modification of salary information.

SODReasonCodes.Name: A_P3+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : No user should have access to two consecutive stages within the HR flow.
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : No user should have access to two consecutive stages within the HR flow.

SODReasonCodes.Name: A_V1+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : The integrity of SD master data is the basis for the integrity of all transactional data based on it.
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : The integrity of SD master data is the basis for the integrity of all transactional data based on it. Therefore it is strongly recommended having a separate group maintaining the SD master data. Moreover, the combination of master data maintenance with transactional data may encourage fraudulent action by enabling the creating fictitious master data and performing fake transactions on these inappropriate master data. Example: - A user could change the product price, process a sales order, and then reinstate the original price.

SODReasonCodes.Name: A_V3+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : No user should have access to two consecutive stages within the SD flow.
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : No user should have access to two consecutive stages within the SD flow. Examples: - Inappropriate goods deliveries could be concealed by manipulating both the sales order and delivery information. - Payments for unauthorized sales orders could be triggered by creating billing documents for these sales orders to start the billing process. - A user could release orders in suspense hold without consent of Finance. - A user could accidentally or intentionally ship a wrong quantity of goods.

SODReasonCodes.Name: A_X1+
SODReasonCodes.Description: SOX : The registration of the logistical flows should be segregated from the registration of purely financial flows.
SODReasonCodes.Comment: SOX : The registration of the logistical flows (e.g. goods receipts, goods issue, shippings, inventory management, etc.) should be segregated from the registration of purely financial flows. Example: - Fictitious goods receips and/or invoices could be entered, causing the three way match between PO, invoice and goods receipt to be complete and causing the payment to be released and executed through the automatic payment run.

Queries.Risk: With this authorization it is possible carry out a Fiscal year change (ACTVT 35) and a Year-end closing (ACTVT 36) in Asset Accounting.

Queries.Comment: This authorization object defines whether the user is authorized to carry out the following periodic processing in Asset Accounting: Post depreciation (ACTVT 30) Recalculate depreciation (ACTVT 31)
Queries.Risk: Depreciation of assets ensures proper fixed assets book values, depreciations must be calculated accurately and booked timely to the correct asset in order to meet this requirement. As depreciations are expenditures, inaccurate, incomplete or non timely calculation and posting leads to incorrect profit and loss statements.

Asset management reports grant access to both information on asset master data and transaction data The asset master record consists of two categories of information: General master data and Depreciation data. General master data includes general information (description, inventory note, last inventory date, etc.), account assignment (which links the record to G/L account information), posting information (capitalization date, acquisition date), time dependent information (business area, cost center, location, plant, etc.), real estate information, leasing conditions (agreement number, length of lease), investment support measures, information on the origins of the asset, Insurance data and evaluation groups. Depreciation related information contains depreciation key (kind of depreciation), useful life, ordinary depreciation start date, change over year (when changing from declining balance to straight-line method), index (calculate annually increasing replacement values), variable depreciation amounts, and scrap value. Transaction data are all other transactions posted to the asset like yearly depreciations, revaluations, transfers, … Unauthorized or inappropriate display access to these data may lead to inappropriate disclosure of information on corporate assets

Users with access to asset transfer can shift assets between different locations within an organization, incorrect transfers may lead to poor fixed asset inventory records and increase risks that assets are removed from the corporate ledgers which is an activity that is fraud sensitive, especially for assets that can be used in civil life or that can be sold to interested parties.

Asset classes play an important role in the overall scheme of asset management. Asset classes are the main criterion for classifying assets by business and legal requirements. For each asset class, control parameters and default values can be defined for the calculation of depreciation and other master data. Each asset master record must be allocated to one asset class.
Asset classes, for example, include: ·assets under construction ·low-value assets ·leased assets ·financial assets ·technical assets
Using asset classes establishes the link between asset master records (AA) and General Ledger Accounts (FI).
Field elements defined at the asset class level are: ·Account Allocation Key (determines which general ledger accounts are used) ·Number Range ·Master record screen layout ·Default values for asset master record fields ·Control parameters dependent on the asset type ·Depreciation area screen layout and default values ·Depreciation area selection dependent on asset class

The asset master record consists of two categories of information: General master data and Depreciation data. General master data includes general information (description, inventory note, last inventory date, etc.), account assignment (which links the record to G/L account information), posting information (capitalization date, acquisition date), time dependent information (business area, cost center, location, plant, etc.), real estate information, leasing conditions (agreement number, length of lease), investment support measures, information on the origins of the asset, Insurance data and evaluation groups. Depreciation related information contains depreciation key (kind of depreciation), useful life, ordinary depreciation start date, change over year (when changing from declining balance to straight-line method), index (calculate annually increasing replacement values), variable depreciation amounts, and scrap value.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - incorrect valuation of assets due to wrong depreciations - unnoticed removal (theft) of asset master records - increase fraud sensitivity - incorrect fixed assets physical inventory and possible compliance issues (legal - proof of ownership, tax and investment deductions, Sales & Use Tax, regulatory, )

Process orders are the main element used for the detailed planning and execution of process manufacturing. A process order describes the production of batches (materials) in a production run or the rendering of services. It is generated from the master recipe and contains all the information specified during process planning. You use a process order to plan the quantities, dates, and resources of the manufacturing process, to control process order execution, and to define rules for the account assignment and settlement of the costs incurred. In PP-PI, process orders perform the same function as production orders in PP. Erroneous and/or unauthorized changes to process orders directly impacts the production process.

Queries.Description: PP: Maintain Sales and Operations Planning
Queries.Risk: Planned independent requirements are used to perform Demand Management functions. A planned independent requirement contains one planned quantity and one date, or a number of planned independent requirements schedule lines, that is, one planned quantity split over time according to dates. Planned independent requirements can be automatically copied from sales and operations planning. Erroneous and/or unauthorized changes to sales and operations planning data can lead to incorrect forecasts and consequently to incorrect production schedules and economic loss.

Together with bills of material and routings, work centers belong to the most important master data in the R/3 production planning and control system. Work centers are used in task list operations and work orders. Task lists are, for example routings, maintenance task lists, inspection plans and standard networks. Work orders are created for production, quality assurance, plant maintenance and for the Project System as network.
Erroneous and/or unauthorized changes to work centers can lead to incorrect scheduling and capacity planning, to incorrect cost calculations and to production losses.

Queries.Comment: The functions in the Manual Accruals component are based on the Accrual Engine tool. The processes for calculating and posting accruals are made in the Accrual Engine. You enter the data for your accruals in Manual Accruals. A distinction is made here between the following data: · Master Data The master data specifies an accrual transaction in more detail. For example, it contains information about the type of accrual in question (rent, licenses, and so on). The master data remains in the Manual Accruals component. · Posting Data The posting data is required to calculate and post the accruals. This data is transferred to the Accrual Engine. The processes for calculating and posting accruals take place exclusively in the Accrual Engine. Accrual Engine Documents: The Accrual Engine calculates and posts the accruals. Accrual Engine documents are generated when you post the accruals. If you execute an accrual run to post the accruals, Accrual Engine documents are created and then transferred to Accounting automatically. The corresponding Accounting documents are then created in Accounting.

Queries.Comment: Preliminary postings are known in SAP R/3 as parked documents. Parked documents can be used to enter and store incomplete documents. Parked documents can be completed, checked and posted at a later date by a different entry clerk. Parked documents are often used for supervisory review. Parked documents do not update any data in the system, except for cash management.
Queries.Risk: Unauthorized or inappropriate use of this functionality can have consequences like: - Material errors or misstatements in the financial statement en management reporting due to incomplete recording of assets and liabilities - Recording of transactions in the wrong accounting period.

Queries.SuggestedControls:
To help you some SAP standard reports can be run : the reports : S_ALR_87012086 - Vendor List / S_ALR_87012179 - Customer List give you a list of vendors / customers - check mark the box of "dunning data" to ge the dunning info. The tansaction EWFM (report RFEWC150) checks the completion of dunning runs and the printing of dunning notices. If the reports are not detailed enough then a query or quickview could be created.
Implementation of the dual control can help to check sensitive - critical fields. (if dunning is considered as critical in your company)

Queries.Comment: The invoice verification functionality should be restricted to the Accounts Payable department.
Queries.Risk:
When a vendor’s invoice is received, it can be entered through either the Materials and Management Module (MM) or the Financial Accounting Module (FI). However, invoices should not be entered FI unless there is no corresponding PO or GR. Invoices must be entered through MM for matching of the PO, GR and Invoice. Invoice Verification in Materials Management serves the following purpose: It completes the materials procurement, it allows invoices that do not originate in materials procurement (e.g. services, expenses, course costs, etc.) to be processed And it allows credit memos to be processed, either as invoice cancellations or discounts.
Different types of invoice verification exist: Purchase Order Based (All the items of a PO can be settled together, regardless of whether an item has been received in several partial deliveries. All the deliveries are totaled and posted as one item), Goods Receipt Based: (Each individual goods receipt is invoiced separately), Invoice without reference (When there is no reference to a PO, it is possible to post the transaction directly to a material account, a G/L account or an asset account), Evaluated Receipts Settlement (ERS) (The “invoice” is replaced by ERS - updates that would have occurred when the invoice was processed now takes place when the GR is processed)
Posting invoices via MM results in: debit to GR/IR is the quantity received multiplied by the purchase order price, price differences between the PO and the invoice are recorded in a separate account configured for the invoice verification process, usually cash discounts or some similar account. Ideally, in the GR/IR account the debit from the invoice posting should exactly offset the credit from the receipt posting.
Posting invoices (especially the release of blocked invoices) is an important control point in the purchasing cycle. Posting invoices is one element in the 3-way matching between purchase order, goods receipt and invoice. The access to posting invoices and releasing blocked invoices must thus be well controlled.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to Invoice posting functionality can lead to incorrect of unjustified payments of invoices and increases fraud vulnerability.
Queries.ControlObjective: You should set up tolerance for the booking of differences between good receipt quantity and purchase order quantity and the purchased price on the purchase order and the invoice. You should check invoice numbers allocated twice (or more) with same document amout and / or same document date. You should check that you have no gaps in the document number assignment. You should check all "parked" invoices.
Queries.SuggestedControls: To help you some SAP standard reports can be run : MIR5 - Display List of Invoice Documents - MIR6 - Invoice Overview S_ALR_87012341 - Invoice Numbers Allocated Twice / S_ALR_87012340 - SAP Minimal Variant S_ALR_87012342 - Gaps in Document Number Assignment. Use the transaction FBV2-FBV3 to check for Parked invoices or S_ALR_87012992 - List of Parked Documents.

FI-AP records and administers the accounting data for all vendors. Outstanding payables are settled by the payment program. This program supports all the standard payment methods (checks, transfers etc.) in printed form as well as in electronic form (data medium exchange on diskette and data transmission). Respective country specific payment methods can also be configured. The review of the Payment Proposal List & Exception List is very important before the actual payment run is executed. SAP allows manual cheques to be created (e.g. for emergency payments, expenses etc). Invoices to be paid are processed in the FI module using document type “KR.” Access to this document type by general ledger accountants posting journal entries should be restricted, as the ability to choose this document type when posting a GL entry (for example, using transaction F-02) could enable an accounting clerk to enter a fraudulent invoice using a normal G/L transaction, which could be subsequently processed in the payment run.
Via the use of FI documents, direct modifications to the accounts payable records can be made with possible direct P&L bottom line impact.

The payment run is the last stage before payment orders leave the organization. Although SAP provides numerous features, both inherent and configurable, excess access to the payment functionality seriously increases risks for fraud or abusive use of corporate funds.
SAP allows changes to be made to the details held in the proposal run. All changes are only valid within the proposal and do not affect the original documents. Appropriate controls should ensure that changes performed are reasonable and complete. Fields that are changeable include:· Payment (payment method, house bank detail, etc.); and ·Paid items (block indicators, cash discounts, etc.)

Queries.Description: FI-AR: Maintain A/R Extended Manual Postings (beyond posting period)
Queries.Risk:
Receipts from Customers are the final step in the order to cash cycle.
Basic functions The Accounts Receivable component of the FI system records and administers the accounting data of customers. It is also an integral part of sales management. All postings in Accounts Receivable are also recorded directly in the General Ledger; different G/L accounts are posted to according to the transaction involved (for example, receivables, down payments, bills of exchange etc.) The system contains a range of tools that you can use to monitor open items; for example, account analyses, alarm reports, due date lists and a flexible dunning program. Receipts information from customers can come from a variety of sources including bank lockbox, account statement or check deposit list, manually, or directly from customer via EDI. The function of recognizing these receipts from customers and the subsequent matching of those receipts to the appropriate open item is facilitated within SAP through the use of Payment Advices.
Partial or Residual Payments If an incoming payment does not match the original invoice exactly, partial payments or residual payments can be used. A partial payment leaves the original invoice intact and creates a negative amount in the account for the amount of the partial payment. No items are cleared at that time. A partial payment can refer to one or more open items. A residual payment clears the original invoice and creates a new open item for the difference between the payment and the original invoice. This new open item has a current date and can affect the aging. Via the use of FI documents, direct modifications to the accounts receivable records can be made with possible direct P&L bottom line impact Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to payment processing functionality can have consequences like: - negative impact on the client satisfaction when unjustified dunning is performed. - lost revenue through increased fraud vulnerability when payments are not processed immediately to the organizations bank accounts but via an employee account who can cash interests on these sums.

Queries.Description: FI-AR: Maintain A/R Postings with Clearing
Queries.Risk:
Receipts from Customers are the final step in the order to cash cycle.
Basic functions The Accounts Receivable component of the FI system records and administers the accounting data of customers. It is also an integral part of sales management. All postings in Accounts Receivable are also recorded directly in the General Ledger; different G/L accounts are posted to according to the transaction involved (for example, receivables, down payments, bills of exchange etc.) The system contains a range of tools which you can use to monitor open items; for example, account analyses, alarm reports, due date lists and a flexible dunning program. Receipts information from customers can come from a variety of sources including bank lockbox, account statement or check deposit list, manually, or directly from customer via EDI. The function of recognizing these receipts from customers and the subsequent matching of those receipts to the appropriate open item is facilitated within SAP through the use of Payment Advices.
Partial or Residual Payments If an incoming payment does not match the original invoice exactly, partial payments or residual payments can be used. A partial payment leaves the original invoice intact and creates a negative amount in the account for the amount of the partial payment. No items are cleared at that time. A partial payment can refer to one or more open items. A residual payment clears the original invoice and creates a new open item for the difference between the payment and the original invoice. This new open item has a current date and can affect the aging. Via the use of FI documents, direct modifications to the accounts receivable records can be made with possible direct P&L bottom line impact Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to payment processing functionality can have consequences like: - negative impact on the client satisfaction when unjustified dunning is performed. - lost revenue through increased fraud vulnerability when payments are not processed immediately to the organizations bank accounts but via an employee account who can cash interests on these sums.

Preliminary postings are known in SAP R/3 as parked documents. Parked documents can be used to enter and store incomplete documents. Parked documents can be completed, checked and posted at a later date by a different entry clerk. Parked documents are often used for supervisory review. Parked documents do not update any data in the system, except for cash management.
Unauthorized or inappropriate use of this functionality can have consequences like: - Material errors or misstatements in the financial statement en management reporting due to incomplete recording of assets and liabilities - Recording of transactions in the wrong accounting period.

SAP allows changes to be made to the details held in the proposal run. All changes are only valid within the proposal and do not affect the original documents. Appropriate controls should ensure that changes performed are reasonable and complete. Fields that are changeable include:· Payment (payment method, house bank detail, etc.); and ·Paid items (block indicators, cash discounts, etc.)

Queries.Description: FI-GEN: Maintenance Balance and P&L Accounts Structure
Queries.Risk:
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes in the financial statement versions may result in inaccurate financial reporting.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes in the financial statement versions makes organizations more vulnerable to fraud.
The financial statement version forms the basis for creating financial statements. Using the financial statement version allows organization to specify:
- items to be included in the financial statements and the sequence in which they are listed in the statements - item texts and the language in which they should be printed - charts of accounts and the individual accounts that are relevant to the financial statements. Accounts can be assigned to financial statement items according to the account balance - The totals that are to be presented in the statements (display group totals or graduated totals). - other specifications using selection criteria and parameters in the financial statement program.
Several financial statement versions can be defined. This may be necessary to generate the financial statements using different formats set up according to various criteria for commercial purposes, for tax purposes and for internal purposes.
Financial statements can be used in various ways according to specific requirements like. - Per organizational units, for example, the corporate group, a company code or a business area. - In different languages, for example, in the local language used at a subsidiary (company code) or in the language of the corporate group. - Balance sheets stated in different currencies or according to a specific currency type e.g. to create a consolidated balance sheet for a group of company codes with different local currencies or if transactions are recorded in other additional currencies then the company code currency. - Choice between different types of balance sheet, e.g. an opening balance sheet or a closing balance sheet. - Vary the level of detail of financial statements. For the accounting department, it lists the individual accounts with their respective balances. For senior management, it summarizes this information to create a single balance sheet for the whole group.

Posting periods can be open and closed on a company code level and can also be done on an account level, i.e., A/P and A/R can be closed but G/L account can remain open. A period is regarded as technically closed if there is no table entry left that allows a posting for that time interval. It is important that only one posting period remains open forcing the users to post documents in that period only.
Keeping past and future posting periods open may result in financial transactions being posted to an incorrect period as documents can be posted into any open posting period.
According to most GAAP, Accounting records must be kept in sequential order and should be unalterable after closing - revision of or changes to prior period figures only occurs in extraordinary circumstances. Non compliance with these requirements can have serious consequences for management as it could potentially be considered as (attempt to) financial fraud.
Also posting entries in future periods is not allowed under US-GAAP - future events need to be processed via accrual and deferral accounts.
In some countries, where accounting records are used as basis for indirect tax filings (VAT, etc.), also other penalties can result from non compliance with the requirement of sequential recording of entries and non-alterability.

Queries.Description: FI-MD: Mass Maintain Customer Master Data (Finance)
Queries.Comment: This process gives you access to the maintenance of customer on general data and company code data. The company code data should be restricted only to specific individuals within the Finance department / or to the master data team if the maintenance is centralized.
Queries.Risk:
General data is accessible to both sales and distribution (SD) and accounting (company code). It consists of customer-specific details, such as the customer’s name, address, and contact information, bank account and VAT registration numbers. The general data is maintained at the client level. Company code data is for financial accounting information. (like reconciliation account, payment terms, payment method,..)
From a financial viewpoint, there are two levels of a customer master record: General data that is entered once for a client (i.e., address, bank details) Company code data (i.e., reconciliation account) can vary for each company code. Examples of company code data are: Payment transactions, Dunning, Correspondence, Interest calculation,...
If a customer is maintained centrally (at the client level), there is a third level containing Sales information. In the Sales and Distribution module, a customer’s sales, billing, and shipping information can be recorded. (see query: VCUSTA - XCUSTA)
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like:
- negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction - increased vulnerability to fraud, creation of dummy customers, ... - wrong VAT declarations,... - posting on wrong reconciliation account,...
Queries.ControlObjective: You should check all new entries in the customer master data in order to avoid double or triple entries. Some sensitive and critical fields, like Tax information, VAT registration numbers and Bank details should be verified. Some sensitive and critical fields should be set up as mandatory fields to be filled in.
Queries.SuggestedControls: To help you some SAP standard report exist: S_ALR_87012179 - Customer List, S_ALR_87012180 - Address List, S_ALR_87012182 - Display Changes to Customers. If the reports are not detailed enough then a query or quickview could be created. Implementation of the dual control can help to check sensitive - critical fields.

Queries.Comment:
This process give you the access to the maintenance of the general data and the company code data of the vendor master data.
Vendor Master data is stored at three levels: 1. General data applies to every company code and every purchasing organization. The general area includes, for example, the vendor's name, address, language, telephone number, bank account and VAT numbers.. 2. Company code data that is specific to an individual company code. Company code data includes, for example, reconciliation account number and payment terms. 3. Purchasing organization data specific to purchasing organizations and relevant to raising requests for quotations, purchase orders etc. For example - conditions, minimum order value..
Separate transactions and authorizations are available to segregate maintenance of Company Code (Accounting) and Purchasing data. They can also be maintained centrally using a single transaction.
Each vendor must be assigned to an account group. This then determines the account number assignment and screen layouts.
One-time vendor accounts are used for vendors from whom goods are expected only to be procured once or very rarely. Where one-time vendors are required, a separate account group is normally established in conjunction with a one-time vendor master record. The initial screen for the account group includes a flag to specify that the group is for one-time accounts. Since address and bank account details are entered during invoice/order entry a normal segregation of duties does not operate and compensating controls need to be considered. These might include: - Exception reporting of one-time vendor transactions to facilitate independent review - Use of blocking flags to enforce independent release for payment
Queries.Risk: Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - increased vulnerability to fraud, creation of dummy suppliers - sub-optimal use or loss of purchasing power
Queries.ControlObjective: Check all new entries in the vendor master data in order to avoid double or triple entries. Some sensitive and critical fields, like Tax information, VAT registration numbers and Bank details should be defined and checked. Changes on sensitive and critical fields should be monitored. Some sensitive and critical fields should be set up as mandatory fields to be filled in.
Queries.SuggestedControls: Display changes to vendor master data: S_ALR_87012089
Queries.Recommendation: Should be limited to the (De) Central master data maintenance Team. The company code views, if no master data maintenance team, should be limited to Accounts Payable department.

Queries.Risk:
Posting and purchasing blocks are maintained via transactions like: - FK05 Master records >Block/unblock (from AP menu) - MK05 Master records >Block/unblock (from Purchasing menu) - XK05 Master records > Maintain centrally >Block/unblock
Vendors can be blocked for nominated companies or purchasing organizations or across the board. Additional purchasing blocks are available where Quality Management is used. Payment blocks are established directly through vendor master maintenance (under company code - payment transactions segment).
Standard report RFMAHN03 lists blocked accounts.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - increased risk for unwanted vendors being used - increased risk for payments towards blocked vendors (e.g. for quality problems, pending law suites, …)

Queries.Comment:
This process give you the access to the creation of the general and the company code data of the vendor master data.
Vendor Master data is stored at three levels: 1. General data applies to every company code and every purchasing organization. The general area includes, for example, the vendor's name, address, language, telephone number, bank account and VAT numbers.. 2. Company code data that is specific to an individual company code. Company code data includes, for example, reconciliation account number and payment terms. 3. Purchasing organization data specific to purchasing organizations and relevant to raising requests for quotations, purchase orders etc. For example - conditions, minimum order value..
Separate transactions and authorizations are available to segregate maintenance of Company Code (Accounting) and Purchasing data. They can also be maintained centrally using a single transaction.
Each vendor must be assigned to an account group. This then determines the account number assignment and screen layouts.
One-time vendor accounts are used for vendors from whom goods are expected only to be procured once or very rarely. Where one-time vendors are required, a separate account group is normally established in conjunction with a one-time vendor master record. The initial screen for the account group includes a flag to specify that the group is for one-time accounts. Since address and bank account details are entered during invoice/order entry a normal segregation of duties does not operate and compensating controls need to be considered. These might include: - Exception reporting of one-time vendor transactions to facilitate independent review - Use of blocking flags to enforce independent release for payment
Queries.Risk: Unauthorized or inappropriate creations to these master data can have consequences like: - increased vulnerability to fraud, creation of dummy suppliers - sub-optimal use or loss of purchasing power
Queries.ControlObjective: Check all new entries in the vendor master data in order to avoid double or triple entries. Queries.Description: CO: Maintain Cost Center Actual Assessments & Actual Distributions
Queries.Risk:
Line item posting is CO can result in: · Cost transfers between Cost Elements (cost types) · Cost transfers between Cost Objects (cost centers)
As controlling areas do not necessarily match with company codes and legal entities, such entries may cause inter-company impacts with possible legal impact (Sales and Use Tax, VAT, …) and should be performed by persons knowledgeable of the consequences.
If more than one company code is assigned to a controlling area, it is possible to allocate costs from one cost center to a cost center assigned to a different company code. Such cross company allocations result in an imbalance between CO totals and FI totals. The reconciliation ledger identifies such transactions and reports the net difference between FI and CO for the period. It can be configured to post these differences to FI automatically, or may be used for informational purposes (and subsequent manual adjustment).
The reconciliation ledger is what makes cross company code cost accounting possible. Because legal reporting is based in FI, all transactions that cross company codes in CO must be reflected in FI. This ledger captures the cross company CO transactions and allows an automatic entry to be posted to FI to get CO and FI back in sync.
The reconciliation ledger records the account, company code, business area, functional area, cost element, object type (cost center, order, project, etc.), object class (O/H management, investment, production, profitability analysis), transaction, dr/cr, COAr currency, company code currency, group currency, and quantity.
If an FI-related boundary is crossed in CO, such as when a cost center allocates its costs to other cost objects in different company codes, the reconciliation ledger keeps track of this. A reconciliation posting can then be made at the end of the period to bring FI and CO in sync.
Errors in the classification of costs or deliberate omissions may lead to erroneous budgeting for future periods and poor management decision support information

Queries.Description: CO: Execute Cost Center Actual Assessments & Actual Distributions
Queries.Risk:
Cost elements represent specific cost types incurred by the organization. There are two types of cost elements: –Primary cost elements Must exist as G/L accounts (P&L expense accounts). They originate from outside the CO module (i.e. posted through FI). Primary cost elements have counter-parts in FI and are used as a method for moving costs into the CO module. –Secondary cost elements originate from within CO and have no FI counter-part. Secondary cost elements are used as a tool for moving costs for internal reporting within CO. They exist exclusively in CO.
Primary Cost Elements mirror costs originally posted to an FI P&L account. All FI P&L expense accounts should be mapped into CO as primary cost elements. In this way, all cost activity originating in FI will be captured by the CO system, note that primary cost elements may also be revenues. Typically, however, revenues are accumulated and analyzed using other CO modules such as OPA, PA or PCA.
Without primary cost elements, costs would not flow into CO from other modules.
Movement of costs between CO cost objects are carried out through secondary cost elements. Secondary cost elements do not have counter-parts in FI. They originate from within the CO module and are not reported in the external financial records. Secondary costs serve primarily as allocation and settlement vehicles, used when the costs of one or more cost objects must be allocated to one or more other cost objects. The basis for the distribution is a statistical key figure.
The are 2 allocation methods: - Assessments: where the costs from the original cost elements (both primary and secondary) are grouped together into assessment cost elements (specific type of secondary cost element), which allocate costs between the sending and receiving cost centers. - Distribution: where the original primary cost elements are used to allocate costs between sending and receiving cost elements.
Errors in the classification of costs or deliberate omissions may lead to erroneous budgeting for future periods and poor management decision support information

Queries.Description: CO: Maintain Cost Center Hierarchy Master Data
Queries.Risk:
Each cost center is assigned to a superior hierarchy area in its master record. The area represents a group of several cost centers. Areas can be grouped into superior levels, forming a hierarchy of areas and cost centers (on the lowest level of the hierarchy).
One hierarchy must be designated as the standard hierarchy. All cost centers you create must be assigned to one area in this standard hierarchy. This assures that all cost centers of the controlling area are combined within a standard hierarchy.
Any number of alternative hierarchies can be parallel to each other - called cost center groups. These give another way to report, group and view costs. When a cost center is created, a node (placement) must be put in the master record for the assignment to standard hierarchy.
Maintain access to Master data should be strictly limited and based on business requirements.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - Errors in management reporting may lead to incorrect business decisions - Decreased confidence of management in management information provided.

Queries.Description: CO: Maintain Cost Center Master Data
Queries.Risk:
The cost center is the smallest unit responsibility within a company and is embedded in the company’s overall organizational structure. This structure is reflected in the CO-CCA system. Each time a cost center is created it must be assigned to a cost center group within the standard hierarchy. This ensures that all cost centers within a particular controlling area are grouped together.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - Errors in management reporting may lead to incorrect business decisions - Decreased confidence of management in management information provided.

Funds reservation enables the allocation of budgets to specific cost objects in CO being a cost center, an internal order, … Errors in the allocation of budgets or deliberate omissions may lead to erroneous budgeting for future periods, poor management decision support information and weaker control possibilities The importance of this functionality becomes even more important when budget availability checking and earmarked funds are used to in the approval process of purchase requisitions and purchase orders.

Cost center planning aims at planning the types of costs and associated dollar amounts that are expected to be incurred for the planning period within a cost center. Unlike planning and budgeting which is a top-down process, it is a bottom-up process and a component of short term (usually a fiscal year) corporate planning. Cost center planning provides tools to management to control expenses and monitor effectively. Errors in the classification of costs or deliberate omissions impairs the quality of management controls and could leave frauds undetected.

Cost element planning aims at planning the types of costs and associated dollar amounts that are expected to be incurred for the planning period within a cost center. Unlike planning and budgeting which is a top-down process, it is a bottom-up process and a component of short term (usually a fiscal year) corporate planning. Cost element planning provides tools to management to control expenses and monitor effectively. Access to cost element planning should be granted on need to have basis as knowledge of cost element planning could reveal information on strategic direction, commercial activities, not yet know cost reduction plans or restructuring projects, etc. Unwanted disclosure of such possible sensitive information may have serious negative impact on the organizations financial results and business reputation.

Customizing is a development activity and should be treated as such. Consequently these activities should follow the regular change management principles. Therefore, no permanent maintain customizing access should be granted in a production environment.
In case customizing activities in the production environment are necessary (e.g. Workflow configuration, Objects that cannot be transported,) this access should be temporary in nature and well controlled. In addition, specific review, test and acceptance procedures should be in place.
In all other case, access to customizing in production, should be display only.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to configuration elements make organizations more vulnerable to fraud as these elements like configurable controls are essential parts of the internal controls framework embedded in the system.

Queries.Description: CO: Maintain Internal Order Closing Activities
Queries.Risk:
OPA functionality is used primarily for events that take place within a company. Typically, such events are self contained or otherwise unique in some way. Examples of activities that could be supported by internal orders include trade fairs, repairs, marketing campaigns and capital spending.
Revenue and cost information may be posted to internal orders to facilitate “complete picture” reporting of the unique event or circumstance represented by the order. Although this is also true of cost centers, typically only cost information is posted to cost centers and revenue information is collected and analyzed using other modules, such as CO-PA or EC-PCA.
Errors in the classification of costs or deliberate omissions may lead to erroneous budgeting for future periods and poor management decision support information

Queries.Description: CO: Maintain Profit Center Actual Assessments and Distributions
Queries.Risk:
Profit centers typically represent a high-level division of a company. It may represent a particular business, division or product line. Profit centers often represent lines of business while cost centers are typically used to represent the internal components within these lines of business. PCA may be used to produce internal balance sheets and P&L Statements for divisions of an organization that are lower than the Company Code level, thus can be used in place of FI - Business Area functionality.
Errors in profit center accounting may lead to erroneous setting of sales objectives per area. In addition it may lead to erroneous budgeting for future periods and poor management decision support information.

Queries.Comment: This access should be restricted to the Cost Accounting department only.
Queries.Risk:
Product Costing is a sub-module of the Controlling module. The data used to generate a product cost comes from various sources. A product cost is the total of raw material cost, labor cost and overhead cost. The idea is that product costs are a by-product of the efficiency of production. Therefore, it is the production master data which defines the product costs.
Total raw material cost is the standard quantity of raw materials to be used (from the bill of material - PP master data) times the cost of raw material (material master - MM master data). The labor cost may come from a cost center (CO master data) which can be allocated to products by an activity type (CO master data) through a routing (PP master data). Overhead may be allocated to products in a number of ways. Like labor costs, it can be allocated by cost center/activity type (CO master data) through a routing (PP master data). It can also be allocated as a percentage of other costs via a costing sheet (CO configuration).
Since every piece of a product cost is an allocation or a standard cost, the only way to determine if standards are accurate is to compare them to actual production costs. Therefore, the production order is the means to track actual costs that went into production vs. the standard cost that was generated for the product. The difference is variance. Due to the various master data involved, security and procedures over this data are key control points.
Costs accumulated on the production order: Raw Materials/ Semi manufactured Goods issued, Labour confirmation, Overhead allocation Credit ed for Finished Goods receipt, Difference is variance
Errors in product costing may lead to erroneous setting of sales prices and could cause serious losses when focus from the sales force is set at low value added products with are not recognized as such from CO-PC. In addition it may lead to erroneous budgeting for future periods and poor management decision support information

When entering the goods issue of a material handled in batches the system can use a specific search strategy to find batches with certain characteristic values (such as status, shelf life, etc.) and suggests these batches in a list. The system suggests how to distribute the given quantity to the batches found. You can accept the system’s proposal for the goods movement or you can distribute the quantity manually.
Incorrect and/or unauthorized batch search strategies can lead to erroneous batch proposals by the system and to erroneous goods issues.
Clearing of incorrect inventory differences can lead too erroneous and/or fraudulent inventory figures.

Unauthorized or inappropriate changes in the configuration elements may result in inaccurate financial reporting.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes in the configuration elements makes organizations more vulnerable to fraud by employees as configurable controls like tolerance limits could be circumvented.
It is good practice to treat customizing as a development activity and to apply the same generally accepted change management procedures to customizing. Therefore, no permanent maintain customizing access should be granted

To designate a material in your warehouse as dangerous, you must first create a hazardous material record and then assign it to the material master record of the dangerous material. When a material master record is linked to a hazardous material record and the hazardous material storage checks have been activated, characteristics defined in the hazardous material record are then taken into consideration for storage type and storage section search.
Incorrect and/or unauthorized maintenance can lead to inadequate storage of hazardous materials, potentially exposing warehouse employees to danger and potentially leading to litigations and non compliance with regulations.

Organisations must carry out a physical inventory of their warehouse stocks at least once per fiscal year to balance its inventory. To meet this legal requirement, various procedures and techniques can be implemented. The SAP System supports the following physical inventory procedures: periodic inventory, continuous inventory, cycle counting and inventory sampling
In the SAP System, physical inventory can be carried out both for a company's own stock and for special stock. Inventory for a company's stock and for special stocks (e.g, consignment stock at customer, external consignment stock from vendor or returnable packaging) must be taken separately (in different physical inventory documents). Furthermore, the stock can be divided into stock types. In the standard system, a physical inventory can be carried out for the following stock types: unrestricted-use stock in the warehouse, stock in quality inspection and blocked stock
Inventory of all stock types mentioned can be taken in a single transaction. For the materials to be inventoried, one item is created in the physical inventory document for every stock type. Physical inventory takes place at storage location level. A separate physical inventory document is created for every storage location. Please note that the post of physical inventory differences also creates goods movements: Goods receipts for increases in stock levels and Goods issues for decreases in stock levels
As physical inventory relates to tangible goods that can be more or less vulnerable to theft, it is key that the different steps in the process are properly separated – basically the access to the physical goods and the record in the system containing information should be properly restricted and segregated.
Unauthorized and/or unqualified access to physical inventory functionality can jeopardize the integrity of the inventory records and stock data (quantities and values) and of the production cycle. It also makes organisations more vulnerable to theft and fraud. Postings of incorrect inventory differences can lead too erroneous and/or fraudulent inventory figures.

Picking with Warehouse Management allows you to use the transfer order as the picking order.
Erroneous and/or unauthorized picking transactions can lead to incorrect and/or fraudulent goods movements.

Although you can initiate some material status changes within Warehouse Management (WM), posting changes are generally initiated in the IM application component as transfer postings and then subsequently processed in WM. When you initiate a transfer posting in IM, the system creates a posting change notice in WM. Posting change notices are only relevant for materials tracked within WM that have undergone a change in status. To finalize the process, you create and confirm a transfer order for the posting change notice in WM.
Erroneous and/or unauthorized posting change notices can lead to incorrect transfer orders and to incorrect goods movements.

Queries.Description: WM: Maintain Production Supply Master Data

Queries.Risk:
When you use the replenishment task, the system calculates the replenishment quantities that are necessary to maintain appropriate stock levels based on the current stock situation for each storage bin and entries in the material master record. The system then creates transfer requirements for the quantities needed. Afterward, you process the transfer requirements to create transfer orders according to the procedures you would normally use to carry out stock movements in WM.
Erroneous and/or unauthorized replenishments can lead to incorrect purchases, incorrect stock transfers and inappropriate stock levels.

A transfer order is a document that contains all the information needed to carry out the physical movement of material into the warehouse, out of the warehouse or from one storage bin to another within the warehouse. Transfer orders are also used to track the logical transfers of stock. Logical transfers of stock occur, for example, when goods are released from inspection and made available for general use.
Erroneous and/or unauthorized transfer orders can result in incorrect goods movement in the warehouses.

Queries.Description: WM: Maintain Transfer Postings in Inventory Management
Queries.Risk:
A transfer posting generally refers to a bookkeeping change - a change in information - about a particular material. For most transfer postings, such as changing a batch number or releasing blocked stock, the goods themselves remain in the same physical location.
Transfer postings are made for several reasons. Some of these include:
- Releasing stock from inspection into available stock - Converting blocked stock to inspection stock - Designating available material as inspection stock - Changing a material number - Splitting available materials into two or more batches - Converting special stock, such as consignment stock or returned stock, into the company's own stock - Changing ownership of stock in the same warehouse from one plant to another
Erroneous and/or unauthorized transfer postings can result in incorrect stock statusses, potentially leading to inappropriate use of these materials because of incorrect information. An example can be the use of materials that did not (yet) pass the quality controls, but that have been incorrectly released based on a wrong transfer posting.

A transfer requirement is a document that is used to plan and initiate stock movements. Using transfer requirements as planning documents, WM creates transfer orders that are then used to execute physical stock movements.
Erroneous and/or unauthorized transfer requirements can lead to incorrect tranfer orders and incorrect physical stock movements.

Queries.Description: WM: Maintain Warehouse Management Master Data
Queries.Risk: Warehouse management master data mainly relates to storage bins (as warehouse numbers and storage types are defined in customizing). All WM transactions are based on this master data. Erroneous and/or unauthorized changes to master data can harm the integrity of all WM data based on it.

Queries.Description: MM-IV: Release Blocked Invoices via MRBR
Queries.Comment:
SPEGR - Blocking reason
I - Quality M - Quantity P - Price Q - Manually S - Other G - Order Price Quantity T - Date V - ???
Queries.Risk:
When a vendor’s invoice is received, it can be entered through either the Materials and Management Module (MM) or the Financial Accounting Module (FI). However, invoices should not be entered FI unless there is no corresponding PO or GR. Invoices must be entered through MM for matching of the PO, GR and Invoice. Invoice Verification in Materials Management serves the following purpose: It completes the materials procurement, it allows invoices that do not originate in materials procurement (e.g. services, expenses, course costs, etc.) to be processed And it allows credit memos to be processed, either as invoice cancellations or discounts.
Different types of invoice verification exist: Purchase Order Based (All the items of a PO can be settled together, regardless of whether an item has been received in several partial deliveries. All the deliveries are totaled and posted as one item), Goods Receipt Based: (Each individual goods receipt is invoiced separately), Invoice without reference (When there is no reference to a PO, it is possible to post the transaction directly to a material account, a G/L account or an asset account), Evaluated Receipts Settlement (ERS) (The “invoice” is replaced by ERS - updates that would have occurred when the invoice was processed now takes place when the GR is processed)
Posting invoices via MM results in: debit to GR/IR is the quantity received multiplied by the purchase order price, price differences between the PO and the invoice are recorded in a separate account configured for the invoice verification process, usually cash discounts or some similar account. Ideally, in the GR/IR account the debit from the invoice posting should exactly offset the credit from the receipt posting.
Posting invoices (especially the release of blocked invoices) is an important control point in the purchasing cycle. Posting invoices is one element in the 3-way matching between purchase order, goods receipt and invoice. The access to posting invoices and releasing blocked invoices must thus be well controlled.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to Invoice posting functionality can lead to incorrect of unjustified payments of invoices and increases fraud vulnerability.

Queries.Comment: M_MATE_PER / AKTPR: 03 = perform initialization
Queries.Risk:
Posting periods can be open and closed on a company code level and can also be done on an account level, i.e., A/P and A/R can be closed but G/L account can remain open. A period is regarded as technically closed if there is no table entry left that allows a posting for that time interval. It is important that only one posting period remains open forcing the users to post documents in that period only.
Keeping past and future posting periods open may result in financial transactions being posted to an incorrect period as documents can be posted into any open posting period.
According to most GAAP, Accounting records must be kept in sequential order and should be unalterable after closing - revision of or changes to prior period figures only occurs in extraordinary circumstances. Non compliance with these requirements can have serious consequences for management as it could potentially be considered as (attempt to) financial fraud.
Also posting entries in future periods is not allowed under US-GAAP - future events need to be processed via accrual and deferral accounts.
In some countries, where accounting records are used as basis for indirect tax filings (VAT, etc.), also other penalties can result from non compliance with the requirement of sequential recording of entries and non-alterability.

Queries.Comment: Customizing should be treated as a development activity and should follow the regular change management principles. Therefore, no maintain customizing access should be granted in a production environment. If access to customizing is necessary, display only access should be enough.
Queries.Risk:
Customizing is a development activity and should be treated as such. Consequently these activities should follow the regular change management principles. Therefore, no permanent maintain customizing access should be granted in a production environment.
In case customizing activities in the production environment are necessary (e.g. Workflow configuration, Objects that cannot be transported,) this access should be temporary in nature and well controlled. In addition, specific review, test and acceptance procedures should be in place.
In all other case, access to customizing in production, should be display only.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to configuration elements make organizations more vulnerable to fraud as these elements like configurable controls are essential parts of the internal controls framework embedded in the system.

Goods movements do not only occur for goods receipts and goods issues, if required, internal stock transfers and transfer postings can occur. Stock transfers and transfer postings are different in the way that with a transfer posting, usually no physical movement of the goods appears. They usually involve a change in stock type, batch number, or material number.
Stock transfers can appear at three different levels: from plant to plant; from company code to company code; and from storage location to storage location.
In general stock transfers from storage location to storage location or from plant to plant can be processed in one step or in two steps. If the One-Step Procedure is applied, only one transaction has to be entered. With the Two-Step Procedure two transactions are required, but “stock in transit” can be monitored. Following are the different input possibilities for stock transfers: From storage location to storage location (notice that no accounting document is created as the stock remains in the same plant and is subject to the same valuation rules), From plant to plant (Accounting is affected if both plants are assigned to different valuation areas and consequently the stock transfer generates a quantity update but and a value update), From company code to company code (procedure is the same as for stock transfers from plant to plant, except that in this case the plants belong to different company codes where 2 in stead of 1 accounting document are created, the offsetting entry for the stock posting is done on a company code clearing account), Transfer Postings (can appear: from material to material and from stock type to stock type) and Stock Transfers with a Stock Transport Order
All physical goods transfers between and within the factories and warehouses are translated into different movement types within SAP. Examples of movement types are: goods receipts, goods to production, obsolete stock, shipping, etc. Movement types have an important control function in Inventory Management. For example, they play a role in updating of quantity field in updating of stock and consumption accounts, and in determining which fields are displayed during entry of a document in the system. Unauthorized and/or unqualified access to movement types can jeopardize the integrity of the inventory records and stock data (quantities and values) and of the production cycle.

Queries.Description: MM-IM: Maintain Goods Receipts for Purchase Orders
Queries.Comment: The goods receipt functionality is a typical Warehouse activity and should be restricted to warehouse employees. The receipt of goods should be segregated from the Shipping Process (goods issues).
Queries.Risk: The goods receipt on purchase orders is another key control point in the purchasing cycle. It is one of the 3 elements in the 3-way match.

Purchasing info records represent the relationship between a specific material or service and a vendor supplying the material or the service.
There are two types of info record: - info records with a material master record (e.g. for stock material). This type of info record represents the relationship between a material or service (for which a master record exists) and a vendor. - info records without a material master record (e.g. for consumable materials). This type of info record represents the relationship between a material or service for which no master record exists and a vendor.
Purchase info records provide the purchasing department with valuable information like general data (e.g. reminders, units of measure), purchasing organization data (e.g. planned delivery time, delivery tolerance limits), pricing conditions (validity period, net price simulations), consignment price information (for vendor consignment material), Order price history (e.g. net price, price variance), Statistics (e.g. quantities and values, number of purchasing documents, delivery statistics) and Texts (e.g. info record texts – internal memo, purchase order text)
Maintenance of purchasing info records can be automated or manual. If the automatic option is chosen, the system ensures the maintenance of the records – e.g. the record points to the most recent purchasing document to determine the price used on a new purchasing document. In case the update is manual, the user must maintain the purchase info record on an on-going basis – e.g. in the current price changes, the user must update the purchasing info record to reflect the new price.
Thus, the info record allows buyers to quickly determine: which materials have been previously offered or supplied by a specific vendor, which vendors have offered or supplied a specific material, which quotation were received and so on.
Other efficiency gains in the proper use of purchasing info record may be e.g. storage of current and future quotation conditions (discounts, fixed costs etc.) in the info record, in order to be able to copy them into PO’s.
Because info records are a key source of information for the purchasing and subsequent logistics processes, incorrect and/or unauthorized info record data can lead to incorrect purchase orders (wrong price, wrong vendor, wrong terms) and can seriously impact the logistics chain and consequently also the financial result of the organization.

In the Inventory Management system, when a goods movement is posted, a material document is generated that serves as proof of the movement and as a source of information for any applications that follow. Unauthorized and/or unqualified access to material documents can jeopardize the integrity of the inventory records and stock data (quantities and values) and of the production cycle. A material document consists of a header and at least one item. The header contains general data about the movement (for example, its date). Each item describes one movement.

Queries.Description: MM: Maintain MRP Long Term Planning
Queries.Risk:
Materials requirements planning (MRP) functionality is used to automate and smoothen the supply chain in organisations, it helps to determine the requirements based on production planning data, purchase information on outstanding orders and order lead times, sales forecasts, etc.. Based on this information, MRP will start the ordering process automatically or propose ordering to the MRP controller.
An MRP controller is a person or group of people responsible for the planning of materials, in a specific material-plant combination. The MRP controller is associated with a material through the material master MRP screen – in most cases, on MRP controller is responsible for a number of materials. The MRP controller selects MRP lists for review and subsequent processing.
From the above it is obvious that correct information on inventory levels is a key success factor for MRP.
Unauthorized and/or unqualified access to MRP functionality can create breaks in the supply chain that can cause delivery problems. The financial consequences of such events can be very important as well as the harm to the business reputation.

Queries.Description: MM-PUR: Maintain Contracts, Outline and Scheduling Agreements
Queries.Risk:
Contracts and Scheduling agreements are two variant of Outline Agreements and are important pieces of Master data in the Requisition to Pay process. A (quantity) contract is an agreement that a supplier to order a certain quantity of a product during a specified period. The contract contains basic quantity and price information but no schedule of specific delivery dates and quantities. The supplier fulfills a contract by placing purchase orders against it. These purchase orders are known as release orders (or call-offs). A release order refers to the relevant contract and the system automatically updates the requested quantities in the contract. Scheduling Agreement - unlike a contract which only contains an overall target quantity or value - a scheduling agreement also contains specific order quantities and delivery dates.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - negative impact on the supplier relationships when requisition schemes are not adhered to and may lead to loss of preferred customer status with suppliers which may lead to price increases.

Inventory for a company's stock and for special stocks (e.g, consignment stock at customer, external consignment stock from vendor or returnable packaging) must be taken separately (in different physical inventory documents). Furthermore, the stock can be divided into stock types. In the standard system, a physical inventory can be carried out for the following stock types: unrestricted-use stock in the warehouse, stock in quality inspection and blocked stock
Inventory of all stock types mentioned can be taken in a single transaction. For the materials to be inventoried, one item is created in the physical inventory document for every stock type. Physical inventory takes place at storage location level. A separate physical inventory document is created for every storage location. Please note that the post of physical inventory differences also creates goods movements: Goods receipts for increases in stock levels and Goods issues for decreases in stock levels
As physical inventory relates to tangible goods that can be more or less vulnerable to theft, it is key that the different steps in the process are properly separated – basically the access to the physical goods and the record in the system containing information should be properly restricted and segregated.
Unauthorized and/or unqualified access to physical inventory functionality can jeopardize the integrity of the inventory records and stock data (quantities and values) and of the production cycle. It also makes organizations more vulnerable to theft and fraud.
Postings of incorrect inventory differences can lead too erroneous and/or fraudulent inventory figures.
