Materials requirements planning (MRP) functionality is used to automate and smoothen the supply chain in organisations, it helps to determine the requirements based on production planning data, purchase information on outstanding orders and order lead times, sales forecasts, etc.. Based on this information, MRP will start the ordering process automatically or propose ordering to the MRP controller.
An MRP controller is a person or group of people responsible for the planning of materials, in a specific material-plant combination. The MRP controller is associated with a material through the material master MRP screen – in most cases, on MRP controller is responsible for a number of materials. The MRP controller selects MRP lists for review and subsequent processing.
From the above it is obvious that correct information on inventory levels is a key success factor for MRP.
Unauthorized and/or unqualified access to MRP functionality can create breaks in the supply chain that can cause delivery problems. The financial consequences of such events can be very important as well as the harm to the business reputation.

Queries.Comment:
MR21 is used for a price change for any materail. Once the material is created and some MM movements have been done on that then you wont be in the position to change the price going to MM02. In such case you need to do if via MR21.
Impact in accounting :
- Changed price would be debited or credited to the stock account depending on the increase or decrease in the price respectively. - Same amount would be posted to loss or proft account depending on the increase or decrease in the price respectively
Queries.Risk:
Using standard SAP, pricing for POs is proposed from the purchasing info record for the vendor material, if it exists, or from the contract, if the PO is a release order. Conditions (in pricing, these are "pricing conditions") determine how the system calculates the net price. E.g. vendor's discounts and surcharges constitute conditions. The net price for the conditions is calculated from the discounts and surcharges defined. In the standard system, appropriate condition types already exist for the following price elements: Duty, Delivery costs, Discount, Price/quantity scale, Surcharge, Provisions, Taxes Purchase price tolerances can be configured and will provide a warning message if purchase price differs from previous by more than a specified tolerance.
The quality of pricing master data influences the quality of transactional data in the SAP system.
Unauthorized / uncontrolled access to pricing master data may compromise the integrity of the transactional data based on it. Especially the stock valuation, cost of goods sold, variances and margins can be affected by incorrect changes of standard prices and may lead to material misstatements in the organizations financial statements and management information. Erroneous management information may lead to incorrect business decisions and can destroy shareholder value.

Queries.Comment:
The creation and maintenance should be reserved for the purchasing department only.
All purchasing process information is stored in documents, grouped per document type (request for quotations, quotations, purchase requisitions, purchase orders, outline agreements,etc.). To segregate the accesses within each of these document types, more specific document types need to be specified.
Queries.Risk:
A purchase order is a formal request to a vendor to provide certain materials or services under certain conditions (quantity, price/pricing conditions, delivery date). Purchase order can be created directly or with reference to an RFQ, a contract, a requisition, or another purchase order. Purchase orders can be created automatically from requisitions. All items on a purchase order must belong to the same company code (determined by the plant assigned to each item). However, it is possible for a purchase order to reference a document created in another company code.
Item categories are used in purchase requisitions / orders to define further requirements or processing of particular items (the configuration of POs and PRs was based on document type). An item category defines whether a purchase order item is: GR valuated (if non-valuated, the GR/IR account is not used and the item will be given financial accounting recognition upon invoice receipt), requires a Goods Receipt (GR) or Invoice Receipt (IR)
Allowable item categories per purchasing document type can be specified in customizing. Individual settings in each item category can be changed and new item categories created, also in customizing.
It is good practice that the GR, GR non-val and GR based invoice verification fields are display only or suppressed.
GR based invoice verification is used primarily where payment is required based on partial receipts. Invoice quantity matching is performed against the goods receipt document rather than the purchase order. It also requires a goods receipt document to be posted before the corresponding invoice can be entered. This could cause cut-off problems if there are delays in posting goods receipts.
Since approvals apply at the purchase order or purchase requisition stage, GR based invoice verification could allow normal delegated authority levels to be bypassed if over deliveries are permitted.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to Purchase order functionality can lead to incorrect of unjustified purchase orders, ultimately this results in commitments to vendors and result in outgoing payments / money leaving the company without valid business reason.

Queries.Description: MM-PUR: Release Purchase Requisitions with Classification
Queries.Comment: Only authorized individuals should have access to this functionality. Note that the release functionality needs to customized / set up. If not, the creation of a purchase requisition automatically results in a released one.
Queries.Risk:
Purchase requisitions are internal request to purchasing where an employee ask the buyer to provide a certain quantity of a material or service on a certain date. Purchase requisition can be entered manually or through MRP. The MRP controller can also convert a planned order into a purchase requisition. Source determination is a separate function. The buyer immediately receives proposals if, e.g. fixed vendors or outline agreements exist for the material.
An electronic approval (release) procedure for purchase requisitions can be implemented. According to certain conditions, the release procedure can determine that a purchase requisition item can only be approved for an RFQ or purchase order if it is released in sequence by certain persons or departments. Purchase requisitions are optional - it is possible for buyers to raise purchase orders directly without referencing a requisition. It is therefore important the release strategies (electronic approvals) also apply at the PO stage.
Important field in the Purchase requisition are: Goods Received and Invoice Received requirements for three way matching may be editable during purchase requisition or order entry. Matching criteria can be set to: “GR”: requiring receipt of goods before any payment processing, “IR”: requiring receipt of invoice before any payment processing; ”GR non-val”: stock is not valuated at time of receipt and is managed by quantity only (no financial accounting recognition is given to goods receipts and this setting turns off the use of the GR/IR account), “GR-based IR”: allows the matching of invoices to individual goods receipts in the case of partial shipments against a PO. Use this option if a separate invoice is received for each good receipt. With this setting, a GR must occur before an invoice can be entered. If the GR flag is not suppressed or display only it allows normal matching controls to be bypassed. Similarly, the GR non-val flag should also not be available under normal circumstances. If business requirements exist for use of this flag it is recommended to defined this at the material master level, with no capability to override during requisitioning.
Release procedures can be implemented to enforce electronic approval of requisitions prior to further processing. Release Strategies include delegation levels and approval sequences based on various characteristics of the requisition like the Release Condition (The conditions for the release of a requisition item may be based on one or a combination of these factors: account assignment category, material group, plant, and the total value), Release Strategy (defines the approval process for requisitions. It defines who must approve a requisition and in what order it is to be approved)
Unauthorized or inappropriate access to Purchase Requisitions and Release procedures makes organizations more vulnerable to fraud by employees as configurable controls could be circumvented.

Queries.Comment: In general, there should be no restriction as to who can create/change purchase requisitions. However, individuals should not have the ability to approve them unless one is authorized to. Note that the release functionality needs to customized / set up. If not, the creation of a purchase requisition automatically results in a released one.

Quotation contains a vendor's pricing and terms of delivery provided in response to an RFQ. It is the basis for selecting the vendor to supply the required material or service.
In MM Purchasing, the RFQ and quotation are the same document. The vendor's pricing and conditions are entered in the original RFQ. This allows using the price comparison list to help determining the best quotation, send rejection letters to the appropriate vendors and store the pricing and terms of delivery for certain quotations in the info record for future reference
Unauthorized creation of or changes to quotations can lead to bypassing the vendor evaluation process within the company. When the vendor evaluation process, aimed at streamlining purchases and maximizing purchasing power does not cover all purchases, risk for non optimal purchasing is increased.

Quotation contains a vendor's pricing and terms of delivery provided in response to an RFQ. It is the basis for selecting the vendor to supply the required material or service.
In MM Purchasing, the RFQ and quotation are the same document. The vendor's pricing and conditions are entered in the original RFQ. This allows using the price comparison list to help determining the best quotation, send rejection letters to the appropriate vendors and store the pricing and terms of delivery for certain quotations in the info record for future reference.
Unnecessary display access to quotations increases the risk for unwanted disclosure of business critical data. This can harm the negotiation position of the organization and could potentially lead to reputation damage. Both consequences cause second line financial losses.

A request for quotation (RFQ) is an invitation to a vendor by a purchasing organization to submit a quotation (bid) for the supply of materials or performance of services.
Unauthorized creation of or changes to request for quotations can lead to bypassing the vendor evaluation process within the company. When the vendor evaluation process, aimed at streamlining purchases and maximizing purchasing power does not cover all purchases, risk for non optimal purchasing is increased.

A request for quotation (RFQ) is an invitation to a vendor by a purchasing organization to submit a quotation (bid) for the supply of materials or performance of services.
Unnecessary display access to request for quotations increases the risk for unwanted disclosure of business critical data. This can harm the negotiation position of the organization and could potentially lead to reputation damage. Both consequences cause second line financial losses.

A request for quotation (RFQ) is an invitation to a vendor by a purchasing organization to submit a quotation (bid) for the supply of materials or performance of services.
Unauthorized creation of or changes to request for quotations can lead to bypassing the vendor evaluation process within the company. When the vendor evaluation process, aimed at streamlining purchases and maximizing purchasing power does not cover all purchases, risk for non optimal purchasing is increased.

Service Master Data can be compared to Material Master Data but for external services instead of materials. Inproper setup of service master data (for example wrong units of measure) can result in erroneous purchase orders.
The receipt of services is another key control point in the purchasing cycle. It is one of the 3 elements in the 3-way match.
The receipt of services is another key control point in the purchasing cycle. It is one of the 3 elements in the 3-way match.

The source list is used in the administration of sources of supply. It specifies the allowed (and disallowed) sources of a material for a certain plant within a predefined period. It indicates the periods during with procurement from sources such as a vendor, an internal plant and an outline agreement are possible. The source list enables MRP to automatically select the scheduling agreement as the single source of supply.
A source list can be maintained manually or via mass changes via the use of the generate function which then reads existing valid purchasing scheduling agreements and purchase info records. To do so, the purchasing view of the material master must be configured to support this generate function.
The source list specifies the validity period, Fixed Vendor (e.g. preferred vendor), outline agreement (contract or scheduling), Blocked Vendor, Usage of MRP regarding vendor (MRP controller)
The MRP controller field has following functions: “ “ – MRP does not read the Source List when processing, “1” – MRP automatically pre-calculates Purchasing Requisitions with the identified contract or scheduling agreement number, “2” – MRP automatically maintains the Delivery Schedules for the identified Purchasing Scheduling agreement.
So basically, the source list serves: - To define a source of supply as "fixed". - To define a source of supply as "blocked". - As an aid in selecting the preferred source during the source determination process. - To block the external procurement of a material.
Erroneous and/or unauthorized changes to source lists can result in: unauthorized purchases of materials from the wrong supplier, sub-optimal purchases due to loss of purchasing power and non compliance with agreed contracts and scheduling agreements. In case unnecessary external purchases are done, the consolidated revenues are decreased and unwanted cash outs occur.

Stock transfers may also be referenced to a stock transport order. The receiving plant would request a material using a stock transport order (similar to a purchase order). The supplying plant would enter a transfer posting to move the stock from unrestricted-use to the receiving plant’s stock-in-transit. The receiving plant receives the goods just as they would if they received goods from a vendor referencing the stock transport order instead of a PO.
The transfer of stock using a stock transport order has the following advantages compared with the transfer of stock without a stock transport order: A goods receipt can be planned in the receiving plant, a vendor (transport vendor) can be entered in the stock transport order, delivery costs can be entered in the stock transport order, stock transport order is included in MRP and Purchase requisitions that were created in MRP can be converted into stock transport orders, the goods receipt can be posted directly to consumption and the entire process can be monitored via the purchase order history.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to transport order functionality can lead to supply breaks, lost goods (property as goods are owned by the organization) and increases fraud vulnerability.

Inventory valuation in the SAP system uses various structures like the Valuation Area that specifies the level at which valuation is organized. This may be specified as plant or company code.
The Valuation Class contains materials with similar properties that have been grouped together for accounting purposes so that they do not have to kept as separate stock accounts for every material. Which valuation class a material can be assigned to depends on the material type. Assignments can be defined in Customizing in 3 ways: All materials with the same material type are assigned to just one valuation class, Different materials with the same material type are assigned to different valuation classes, Materials with different material types are assigned to the one valuation class
A material is assigned to a valuation class in the material master record. The system checks whether the material type allows the material to be assigned to the valuation class specified. The system refers to the valuation class of a material to determine which stock account to post to when a posting is made for this material.
The Valuation Category specifies the criterion according to which split valuation is to be carried out. E.g. Procurement (manufactured in-house or procured externally), Origin (domestic or abroad), Status (new, used, repaired)
Valuation categories are defined in Customization. A material is assigned a valuation category in the material master record.
The Valuation Type specifies the characteristic used for split valuation. The individual characteristics that make up a valuation category are called valuation types. For example, the valuation types in the valuation category Procurement are: internal and external. Valuation types are defined in Customizing. For every material with split valuation, you must enter all the valuation types allowed in the material master record.
Unauthorized and/or unqualified access to inventory valuation functionality can jeopardize the integrity of the inventory records and stock data (quantities and values) and of the production cycle. It also makes organizations more vulnerable to theft and fraud.

Queries.Comment: Should be limited to the Purchasing Department.
Queries.Risk:
Vendor Master data is stored at three levels: 1. General data applies to every company code and every purchasing organization. The general area includes, for example, the vendor's name, address, language, and telephone number. 2. Company code data that is specific to an individual company code. Company code data includes, for example, reconciliation account number and payment terms. 3. Purchasing organization data specific to purchasing organizations and relevant to raising requests for quotations, purchase orders etc. For example - conditions, minimum order value..
Separate transactions and authorizations are available to segregate maintenance of Company Code (Accounting) and Purchasing data. They can also be maintained centrally using a single transaction.
Each vendor must be assigned to an account group. This then determines the account number assignment and screen layouts.
One-time vendor accounts are used for vendors from whom goods are expected only to be procured once or very rarely. Where one-time vendors are required, a separate account group is normally established in conjunction with a one-time vendor master record. The initial screen for the account group includes a flag to specify that the group is for one-time accounts. Since address and bank account details are entered during invoice/order entry a normal segregation of duties does not operate and compensating controls need to be considered. These might include: - Exception reporting of one-time vendor transactions to facilitate independent review - Use of blocking flags to enforce independent release for payment
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - increased vulnerability to fraud, creation of dummy suppliers customers, … - sub-optimal use or loss of purchasing power

Posting and purchasing blocks are maintained via transactions like: - FK05 Master records >Block/unblock (from AP menu) - MK05 Master records >Block/unblock (from Purchasing menu) - XK05 Master records > Maintain centrally >Block/unblock
Vendors can be blocked for nominated companies or purchasing organizations or across the board. Additional purchasing blocks are available where Quality Management is used. Payment blocks are established directly through vendor master maintenance (under company code - payment transactions segment).
Standard report RFMAHN03 lists blocked accounts.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - increased risk for unwanted vendors being used - increased risk for payments towards blocked vendors (e.g. for quality problems, pending law suites, …)

Queries.Description: HR: Reporting (independent check on infotype and org. assignment) (disregard tcode)
Queries.Comment: The P_ABAP object is used to simplify the authorization checks in HR reports for performance reasons. Authorization checks on infotypes via the P_ORGIN object can drastically impact the performance of HR reports. For this reason, SAP has built the P_ABAP object, which bypasses the P_ORGIN checks. From a security perspective, authorizations to P_ABAP should only be granted for specific reports and/or to HR super users.
Queries.Risk:
Granting authorizations for directly starting ABAPs via SA38 implies that the S_TCODE authorizations can be circumvented. Because there is a limited number of objects in the HR module, they are 'shared' by a lot of HR functionality. Therefore, the S_TCODE authorizations provide a required additional barriere to have an adequate security in place. Circumventing this barriere significantly weakens the implemented authorization concept.
Moreover, granting full access to the P_ABAP object circumvents the implemented P_ORGIN authorizations, the central object in securing HR data. The P_ABAP object is meant to be granted to users that already have extensive P_ORGIN authorizations to improve the performance of some reports. This improved performance is achieved by not checking the P_ORGIN restrictions !

Queries.Description: BC: Using of Repository Info System INTERNAL $SEU <4.7 (Alternative)
Queries.Comment: Transaction $SEU allows you to display everything regarding repository: - Tables, views, structures, - Programs, function modules, logical databases, area menus, transactions, message classes, variants, interfaces, - Change requests, Authorization objects, CATT scripts, - Data Modeling, Process Modeling, Business Object Browser, - …
Queries.Risk: The backdoor in this transaction is that dependant of the authorization you have for S_DEVELOP (display activity is sufficient), you can test/execute particular functionality, without having the appropriate transaction (S_TCODE) for it.
Queries.Recommendation: Restrict access to $SEU to an absolut minimum.

Queries.Description: BC: Using of Repository Info System INTERNAL $SEU >4.6 (Alternative)
Queries.Comment: The transaction $SEU only exists in SAP releases lower then 4.7. From of release 4.7 this transaction is replaced by report ‘RS_INFOSYSTEM_START’. Although the transaction $SEU does not exist anymore in 4.7, it’s still possible to call the function module directly: ‘REPOSITORY_INFO_SYSTEM_APPL’. The report or the function module allows you to display everything regarding repository: - Tables, views, structures, - Programs, function modules, logical databases, area menus, transactions, message classes, variants, interfaces, - Change requests, Authorization objects, CATT scripts, - Data Modeling, Process Modeling, Business Object Browser,
Queries.Risk: The backdoor in this transaction is that dependant of the authorization you have for S_DEVELOP (display activity is sufficient), you can test/execute particular functionality, without having the appropriate transaction (S_TCODE) for it.
Queries.Recommendation: Restrict access to that report and the function module to an absolut minimum.

Queries.Recommendation:
* Eliminate all S_BTCH_ADM authorizations in non-technical roles.
* Evaluate which technical roles should have this full background administration authorization.

This authorization allows actions (except releasing) on background jobs of other users.
Queries.Recommendation:
<NA> variant:
* Non-technical users should only be allowed to work with there own background jobs. To allow them to have there own jobs automatically released, they might be given JOBACTION = RELE on the S_BTCH_JOB object. All other, additional authorizations on this object should be removed from all non-technical roles.
ALL variant:
* If needed at all, consider implementing restrictions on jobgroup.

Queries.Risk: CATT procedures can be considered as mass transactions, making multiple changes to data in one session. The quality and integrity control of the input data often lies outside the SAP system. If erroneous data is processed, the error will be in the SAP system for all records in the session.
Queries.Recommendation: * CATT procedures are meant for testing purposes. Consider putting this functionality in a seperate role / profile and assign it more selectively.

Adding a new field to the coding block involves changing central objects in the SAP system, and in particular database tables. Such changes are extremely dangerous, and can lead to inconsistencies throughout your system as well as to a loss of data.

Queries.Description: BC: Debugging Access Update rights (disregard tcode)
Queries.Risk: Debugging with update access allows the user to change internal values, to bypass controls etc. Debugging should not be allowed in production and should only be granted on a really need-to-have basis. The authorizations should be removed immediately when it is not needed anymore.

* Replace this debugging access in change mode at least to display, if not eliminate it completely.

Queries.Risk: Although no confidentiality or integrity risk (no control values can be changed), a debugging session monopolizes a work process in SAP. If debugging sessions are opened extensively and in parallel, the availability of the system could be jeopardized.
Queries.Recommendation: * Review the necessity to have 03 access to the DEBUG object type.

Queries.Risk: Direct development changes in a productive system cause untested functionality to be introduced, cause inconsistencies in your system landscape and can jeopardize the integrity and availability of the productive environment. Development access should therefore be restricted to a development environment only.
Queries.Recommendation:
<NA> variant:
* Eliminate all maintenance accesses out of the S_DEVELOP object.
ALL variant:
* If needed at all, at least implement restrictions on development class and object type in the S_DEVELOP object in the mentioned roles.

Queries.Comment: Please apply S_TCODE YES. An S_TCODE authority check is being programmed in the ABAP.
Queries.Risk: Due to this authorization, users can execute external operating system commands, users can therefore create jobs (in background processing) and execute them.
Regular users should not maintain public holiday definitions, and public holiday and factory calendars.

Queries.Comment: As of BASIS Release 6.40.a user also needs also needs authorization for S_DEVELOP with the new '16' activity ("Execute") to be able to execute function modules,

Queries.Recommendation: * SE37 is a development transaction. Consider putting this functionality in a seperate role / profile and assign it more selectively.

Queries.Risk: To maintain his/her own spools a user only needs transaction code SP01 without any authorizations on the selected objects. If a user's access needs to be extended to spool administrator functions, he/she needs authorizations for SP01 in S_ADMI_FCD In combination with S_SPO_ACT. When you grant this value, a user has access to all spools, also the spools which contain confidential information.
Queries.Recommendation:

* Implement authorization groups for spools with sensitive information and implement restrictions in the SPOAUTH field of the S_SPO_ACT object authorizations.

Queries.Description: BC: IDoc functions update and execute
Queries.Risk:
IDOC's (Intermediate DOCuments) are inbound or outbound interface-messages to or from the SAP system. Access to IDOC traffic leads to acces to the content of the documents which potentially could lead to incorrect or even fraudulent changes.
Protecting IDOCs can only be done on message type, partner number, partner type and direction (inbound or outbound).
Queries.Recommendation: We recommend to tightly restrict access to IDOCs, e.g. to the interface monitoring group. As the process is fully automated only manual interventions are needed to resolve pending and/or rejected Idocs.

Queries.Risk: The described objects with their related authorizations give access to the Implementation Guide. Only a small number of employees should be authorized to generate the enterprise IMG. Moreover, it should never be performed in a production environment. One of the dangers is the performance of the customizing transaction for setting the parameters or change a customizing project.

Queries.Comment: Layouts can be saved user-specifically or for all users. User-specific layouts are only visible for the users who have created them. Layouts for all users can be selected by all users.These layouts always start with a slash in the name (for example /Standard). To be able to save layouts for all users, the user needs the authorization S_ALV_LAYO from Release 4.6C with activity 23. Only with this authorization can you then also branch to the administration of the layouts. Note 409190 also provides further information on the authorizations.
Queries.Risk: Manipulation of Standard Layouts reflects all users, having access to a specific report. Therefore this authorization should be given to only a selected number of users.

BC: Lock and release BIM sessions
BC: Manage lock entries (incl. Deletion of other users locks)

Queries.Description: BC: Use of Local Printer Definitions (disregard tcode)
Queries.Comment: While in non-HR systems access to printers is usually not an issue, this might become the case in an environment with HR functionality. Users printing payroll data or other sensitive HR data could be restricted to certain printers in order to avoid that sensitive data is printed by accident on a remote printer.
Queries.Risk: In this context, the use of local printer definitions (LOCL) constitutes a risk because then the control is transferred to the local Windows settings of the end user’s PC. Switching printers can than be done outside SAP. Specific accesses to printers are controlled via the S_SPO_DEV authorization object.

For each document type a number range is defined, the size of the number range depends of the transaction volume for the document type. Number ranges are assigned either internally (by the system) or externally (by the user). Number ranges, whether internal or external, can be configured to limit user access to certain transactions through the document types.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to the number ranges which are de facto configuration elements make organizations more vulnerable to fraud by employees as configurable controls could be circumvented.

The selected object controls the authorizations to maintain number ranges or to change the usage sequence of a number range. You do not require authorizations for displaying number range objects. This functionality allows users to create gaps in the numbering sequence of accounting documents, etc

Queries.Description: BC: Read access to the operating system files
Queries.Risk:
This filter allows you to audit the extent of access to external (non SAP) files from within ABAP programs. S_DATASET restricts the possible external file access activities (normal or filtered read, normal or filtered write), the ABAP programs from where the external files are accessed and the external file names to be used. These accesses should be limited to expert users.
Example: on UNIX systems, the /tmp/ directory is used as swap memory for the SAP system. Every user file that would be saved in this directy thus limits the available swap memory. Therefore, if granted at all, separate user directories should be created and only those user directories should be authorized via the S_DATASET object.
Queries.Recommendation:
* Evaluate in how far the S_DATASET authorizations in the mentioned roles can be limited to display (ACTVT = 33, A6)
* If granted at all in maintain (ACTVT = 34, A7), the S_DATASET object should be properly restricted on FILENAME and/or PROGRAM.

Queries.Risk:
This filter allows you to audit the extent of access to external (non SAP) files from within ABAP programs. S_DATASET restricts the possible external file access activities (normal or filtered read, normal or filtered write), the ABAP programs from where the external files are accessed and the external file names to be used. These accesses should be limited to expert users.
Example: on UNIX systems, the /tmp/ directory is used as swap memory for the SAP system. Every user file that would be saved in this directy thus limits the available swap memory. Queries.Risk: Profiles and authorizations can be created and/or modified directly in production, which could lead to uncontrolled security breaches and to inconsistencies in the system landscape. Profile and authorization maintenance should follow the regular change management procedures.

Queries.Recommendation:
* Evaluate in how far it would be feasible to apply the regular change management procedures to ABAP query development and maintenance.

Direct table access is the most used backdoor in security.
Queries.Recommendation: * Consider putting this functionality in a seperate role / profile and assign it more selectively.

Queries.Description: BC: Display access to Tables via RFC (disregard tcode)
BC: Execute trusted RFC connections (disregard tcode)
BC: Sys Admin - Reset/delete data without archiving
Queries.Risk: With this authorization, users can delete data without the need of first archiving the data.
Since most ABAPs do not have authorization groups and own developed ABAPs usually lack authority checks, a backdoor is created by giving users access to transaction codes that start ABAPs directly.
Queries.Recommendation:
<NA> variant:
* As a first step, consider putting this functionality in a seperate role / profile and assign it more selectively.
* Investigate for what purposes (what reports, what programs,...) the SA38 tcode is currently used. An option is to use the standard SAP STAD transaction on the productive environment to log all ABAPs started via SA38.
* Implement alternatives for these identified purposes: - for SAP standard ABAPs executed via SA38 find a standard transaction executing the same ABAP (table TSTC) - for SAP standard ABAPs without standard transaction create an own transaction (SE93) - for own developed ABAPs: . create an own transaction that executes the ABAP (SE93) . assign an authorization group to the ABAP (table TRDIR) . includes at least one AUTHORITY-CHECK command
* Give the business an appropriate period of time to give the required information, but put a deadline on the fact that SA38 will be taken away from business profiles.
ALL variant:
* In the affected roles, analyze what tcodes need the S_PROGRAM object.
* For these tcodes, identify the ABAP(s) it is calling.
* For these ABAPs, establish what the authorization groups are.
* Implement these specific authorization groups in the affected roles.

Queries.Comment: The dynamic menu (transaction SDMO) provides a list of all transaction codes, which can be executed without an S_TCODE check.
Queries.Risk:
So, in this scenario one can only rely on the AUTHORITY-CHECK commands within the programs, which may weaken the overall security.
This means that SDMO is very critical transaction.
Queries.Recommendation: Do not allow SDMO access.

Queries.Risk: These transaction codes enable a user to display the table content. Please note that SAP is a table driven application and that all customizing, system settings, application data and master data are stored in tables. Direct table access is the most used backdoor in security
Queries.Recommendation:
<NA> variant:
* As a first step, consider putting this functionality in a seperate role / profile and assign it more selectively.
* Investigate for what tables the SE16 and SE17 tcodes are currently used.
* Implement an alternative for these identified tables: create own parameter transaction codes for the list of specific tables.
* Give the business an appropriate period of time to give the required information, but put a deadline on the fact that the listed transactions will be taken away from business profiles.
ALL variant:
* In the affected roles, analyze what tcodes need the S_TABU_DIS object.
* For these tcodes, identify the tables it is calling.
* For these table, establish what the authorization groups are.
* Implement these specific authorization groups in these affected profiles.

Queries.Comment: For processing a batch input session, one needs authorizations to the underlying objects of the processed transaction(s).
Queries.Risk: Batch input sessions can be considered as a mass transaction, making multiple changes to data in one session. The quality and integrity control of the input data often lies outside the SAP system. If erroneous data is processed, the error will be in the SAP system for all records in the session. Also, processing a same BIM twice can lead to duplicate (fictitious) entries. If confidential data is contained in a BIM, then granting to broad access to all BIMs could lead to confidentiality issues.
Queries.Recommendation:
<NA> variant:
* Reduce the number of users having access to BIMs.
ALL variant:
* For the users that really need it, implement adequate session name restrictions.
* Apply a strong naming convention for session names.

Queries.Comment:
SAP Fix to the original security problem in release 6.10: Additional check on object S_GUI (authorisation for import activity 60) Additional check on S_BTCH_ADM value Y
If required add these additional values to the query!!
Queries.Risk:
Users who can run Batch Input Sessions and at the same time are not limited in S_BTCH_NAM can export a session change the authorised user and import the changed session back into SAP.
When running that imported session in background mode it will use the authorisation of the authorised user and not the user who started the session!.
Queries.Recommendation:
Normal users should not be allowed to have "*" values on S_BTCH_NAM. This recommendation is independent from this SM35 backdoor. Support users who need to be able to appoint batch jobs to different batch users, should not be allowed to run batch input sessions in background mode.
SAP will create an additional activity code for SM35 allowing authorising users for import or export of sessions!

Queries.Description: SD-PR: Maintain Sales Conditions Table (SD Price)
SD-SLS: Maintain Contracts and Rebate Agreements
Queries.Risk:
Contracts and Scheduling agreements are two variant of Outline Agreements and are important pieces of Master data in the Order to Cash process. A (quantity) contract is an agreement that a customer will order a certain quantity of a product during a specified period. The contract contains basic quantity and price information but no schedule of specific delivery dates and quantities. The customer fulfills a contract by placing sales orders against it. These sales orders are known as release orders (or call-offs). A release order refers to the relevant contract and the system automatically updates the released quantities in the contract. Scheduling Agreement - unlike a contract which only contains an overall target quantity or value - a scheduling agreement also contains specific order quantities and delivery dates.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction when delivery schemes are not adhered to and may lead to loss of customers or claims when non timely delivery causes damage. - Increased fraud vulnerability, e.g. dummy transactions to window dress order portfolio, unauthorized price are modifications,..

The contract contains basic quantity and price information but no schedule of specific delivery dates and quantities. The customer fulfills a contract by placing sales orders against it. These sales orders are known as release orders (or call-offs). A release order refers to the relevant contract and the system automatically updates the released quantities in the contract. Scheduling Agreement - unlike a contract which only contains an overall target quantity or value - a scheduling agreement also contains specific order quantities and delivery dates.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction when delivery schemes are not adhered to and may lead to loss of customers or claims when non timely delivery causes damage. - Increased fraud vulnerability, e.g. dummy transactions to window dress order portfolio, unauthorized price are modifications,..

Customizing is a development activity and should be treated as such. Consequently these activities should follow the regular change management principles. Therefore, no permanent maintain customizing access should be granted in a production environment.
In case customizing activities in the production environment are necessary (e.g. Workflow configuration, Objects that cannot be transported,) this access should be temporary in nature and well controlled. In addition, specific review, test and acceptance procedures should be in place.
In all other case, access to customizing in production, should be display only.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to configuration elements make organizations more vulnerable to fraud as these elements like configurable controls are essential parts of the internal controls framework embedded in the system.

Queries.Description: SD-MD: Mass Maintain Customer Master Data (Sales)
Queries.Comment:
This process gives you access to the maintenance of customer on general data and sales organisation data. Sales organisation views should only be given to Customer Service Unit (Dept).
The 'Sold to Party' is a person or company that places an order for goods or services. It can perform the functions of the payer, bill-to party, or ship-to party. The Bill to party' is a person or company that receives the invoice for a delivery or service. The 'Payer' is a person or company that pays the bill. The 'Ship-to Party' is a person or company that receives goods.
Queries.Risk:
Sales area data contains information pertinent to the sales and distribution functions. General data is accessible to both sales and distribution (SD) and accounting. It consists of customer-specific details, such as the customer’s name, address, and contact information, general data is maintained at the client level.
If a customer is maintained centrally (at the client level), there is a third level containing Sales information. In the Sales and Distribution module, a customer’s sales, billing, and shipping information can be recorded.
From a sales viewpoint Sales area data is based on Sales organization, distribution channel, and division. There are separate data screens for sales, shipping, and billing-related data. If two sales organizations sell two product lines (divisions) through three different distribution channels, there still will only be one customer master. However, it will have twelve separate sales views - one for each sales area.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like:
- negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction - increased vulnerability to fraud, creation of dummy customers,... - wrong shipping name or address could cause delivering the goods to wrong address - wrong incoterms could lead problems of responsibilities in terms of transporting the goods
Queries.ControlObjective: You should check all new entries in the customer master data in order to avoid double or triple entries. Some sensitive and critical fields, like Tax information, VAT registration numbers and Bank details should be verified. Some sensitive and critical fields should be set up as mandatory fields to be filled in.
Queries.SuggestedControls:
To help you some SAP standard report exist: S_ALR_87012179 - Customer List, S_ALR_87012180 - Address List, S_ALR_87012182 - Display Changes to Customers. If the reports are not detailed enough then a query or quickview could be created. There is no specific reports to check sales organisation data therefore a report should be created to show all "ship to party", or other partner functions that shows clearly the address, the number, ... and the account group.
As VD?? Transaction codes give access to the general data views, or if the maintenance of customer master data is decentralized,.. then you should define sensitive and critical fields and implement the dual control. (only for general views)

Queries.Comment:
Deliveries and Picking are typical Warehouse activities and should be restricted to warehouse employees. Deliveries and Picking should be segregated from the Receiving Process (goods receipts). Delivery functions Delivery documents are the central documents in the shipping process and essentially represent an authorization to ship. They are used to start all activities relevant to shipping, such as picking, packing, and transporting. The creation of a delivery document alone does not conclude the shipping process. Creation of the delivery document for an order indicates that items may now be picked, packed, etc. As a rule, a delivery is created at one shipping point for an order that is due for delivery. The system copies the relevant data for the order items, that contain the selected shipping point, into the delivery. Once the shipping point is transferred to the delivery, it can no longer be changed. A delivery can be created when the material is due for shipping. This is determined by the material availability date or the transportation planning date, whichever is earlier. The delivery provides the basis for subsequent functions (goods issue, shipment document, billing, etc.).
Delivery document structure A delivery consists of Header and Item level information. Header information applies to the entire delivery document, whereas item-level information applies to each line item. An item in a sales order can consist of several subdivisions according to delivery date and quantity (schedule lines).
Delivery creation deliveries can be created in the following ways: * A specific delivery with reference to an order that already exists in the system. * For all deliveries which are due by monitoring the delivery dates of known orders (processing the delivery due list). Note: The delivery due list is generated by shipping point. * A specific independent delivery without reference to an existing order (should only occur if a stand-alone shipping system is being used).
Queries.Risk: Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to Delivery document processing can have consequences like: - negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction when delivery schemes are not adhered to and may lead to loss of customers or claims when non timely delivery causes damage. - Increased fraud vulnerability

Prior to the receipt of a sales order, the pre-sales cycle can start with an earlier sales query, such as an inquiry or a quotation. Sales queries allow entering and storing of all the important, sales-related information used during sales order processing.
The inquiry represents a general sales query e.g. a customer or prospect wants to know whether you stock a certain line or if catalogues and brochures available for products and/or services.
Quotations can be created when a customer has an informed sales query e.g. a customer or prospect wants to know how much a certain quantity of a product will cost and when it will be available for shipping.
Sales Information documents are used if a customer or prospect wants pricing and delivery information but does not want a written quotation, in this case the contact is recorded as a sales information document. As in the case of an inquiry or a quotation, the sales information document can be used later as the basis for a sales order and sales analysis.
Unauthorized or inappropriate access to inquiries, quotations and sales information documents increases risks of unwanted disclosure towards customers, customer peers or competitors of the organization itself. This may bring harm to the competitive position of the organization who's commercial negotiation possibilities are impaired. Ultimately this may lead to lost revenue due to lower prices in the market and/or loss of customers due to lost confidence or trustworthiness.

After orders have been delivered, they need to be released for billing in order to ensure revenue to be recognized completely and accurately in the proper accounting period.
Unauthorized access to release to billing can cause incorrect billing and invoicing and could influence the incoming revenue stream and lead to incorrect sales figures being presented.

Queries.Comment:
Various methods are available for carrying out picking: * Picking without picking confirmation * Picking with picking confirmation
Picking with picking confirmation: Due to the fact that the system will allow the posting of a goods issue once a delivery is due for goods issue and the picked quantity equals the delivery quantity, problems could arise. Since the delivery quantity is automatically copied into the picked quantity when the pick list is printed, each delivery needs to be verified to ensure that the full quantities have been picked. If not, posting goods issues for incomplete deliveries could occur. Due to the potential problems of the above process, additional functionality has been added to the delivery process in Picking request/confirmation. Picking with picking confirmation entails confirming that the items have actually been picked in the warehouse through the use of a picking confirmation. The primary reason is to prevent accidental goods issue postings after running the picking due list or performing manual picking. For every shipping point, picking confirmation either is mandatory or not.
Picking without picking confirmation: Picking without picking confirmation entails the printing of a picking list which automatically updates the picked quantity to equal the delivery quantity. In this instance, a goods issue can be posted. However, there is nothing to verify that the goods were fully picked. If necessary, the picked quantity is adjusted on the basis of what quantities were actually picked. This situation would involve a manual procedure. One can only post goods issue for a delivery once all items relevant for picking have been fully picked. If the total delivery quantity does not equal the pick quantity, the system either carries out picking again or the confirmed quantity can be copied into the delivery quantity. One can determine to what extent picking has been carried out for a delivery from the picking status. The picking status is stored in each item in the delivery. The following indicators are defined for the picking status:
"_": The item is not relevant for picking A: Picking has not been started B: The item has been partially picked C: The item has been completely picked
Queries.Risk: Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to Picking can have consequences like: - negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction when delivery schemes are not adhered to and may lead to loss of customers or claims when non timely delivery causes damage.

Contracts and Scheduling agreements are two variant of Outline Agreements and are important pieces of Master data in the Order to Cash process. A (quantity) contract is an agreement that a customer will order a certain quantity of a product during a specified period. The contract contains basic quantity and price information but no schedule of specific delivery dates and quantities. The customer fulfills a contract by placing sales orders against it. These sales orders are known as release orders (or call-offs). A release order refers to the relevant contract and the system automatically updates the released quantities in the contract. Scheduling Agreement - unlike a contract which only contains an overall target quantity or value - a scheduling agreement also contains specific order quantities and delivery dates.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction when delivery schemes are not adhered to and may lead to loss of customers or claims when non timely delivery causes damage. - Increased fraud vulnerability, e.g. dummy transactions to window dress order portfolio, unauthorized price are modifications,..

Queries.Description: SD-SLS: Mass Update Currency Sales Documents

Queries.Comment: The shipment of goods is a typical Warehouse activity and should be restricted to warehouse employees. The shipment of goods should be segregated from the Receiving Process (goods receipts).
Queries.Risk:
Shipping of goods to customers or to own warehouses depends on the points from which goods are issued in the company. These are called shipping points. These are the units according to which shipping is organized.
A delivery is processed by one shipping point. This shipping point depends on the: Delivering plant, Shipping conditions (of sold-to party/sales order), Loading group (on material master) Shipping points can process deliveries for more than one plant. A shipping point can be defined according to the material type being shipped. E.g. in the chemical and pharmaceutical industry, hazardous and/or controlled substances are likely to be shipped from a separate shipping point due to the conditions and restrictions of the product. A single shipping point may be used for shipping all different types of material.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to Shipping functionality can have consequences like: - negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction when delivery schemes are not adhered to and may lead to loss of customers or claims when non timely delivery causes damage. - Increased fraud vulnerability

Queries.Comment:
This access should be reserved to the Customer Service Department. However, price overrides should not be done by the Customer Service Department. If this is being done, those changes should be monitored by edit reports.
The processing of credit memos should also be reserved to the Customer Service Department and on a limited basis to the Accounts Receivable department.
Queries.Risk:
Sales orders can be processed in different ways in the system, depending on the organizations specific needs.
The system automatically proposes data from the relevant master records like: sales, shipping, pricing, and billing data from the customer master record of the sold-to party. In addition, the system copies customer-specific master data about texts, partners, and contact people at the customer site. For each material or service in the sales order, the system automatically proposes data from the relevant material or service master records, such as data for pricing, delivery scheduling, availability check, tax determination, and weight and volume determination. The data proposed by the system can act as the basis for a sales order; if sales order processing requires it, these data can be modified manually or new data can be added . E.g., pricing policies may allow to manually change the value of certain discounts within a permitted range. In addition, in the sales order a number of different screens exists where data such as terms of payment and delivery data can be displayed and modified. When processing a sales order using the standard versions of SAP R/3, the system can automatically carry out basic functions, such as the following: Pricing, Availability check (if this function is defined in the material master record), Transferring requirements to materials planning (MRP), Delivery scheduling, Shipping point and route determination, Credit limit check
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to Sales order processing can have consequences like: - negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction when delivery schemes are not adhered to and may lead to loss of customers or claims when non timely delivery causes damage. - Increased fraud vulnerability, e.g. dummy transactions to window dress order portfolio, unauthorized price modifications

If two sales organizations sell two product lines (divisions) through three different distribution channels, there still will only be one customer master. However, it will have twelve separate sales views - one for each sales area.
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like:
- negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction - increased vulnerability to fraud, creation of dummy customers,... - wrong VAT declarations,... - posting on wrong reconciliation account,…
Queries.ControlObjective: You should check all new entries in the customer master data in order to avoid double or triple entries. Some sensitive and critical fields, like Tax information, VAT registration numbers and Bank details should be verified. Some sensitive and critical fields should be set up as mandatory fields to be filled in.
Queries.SuggestedControls: To help you some SAP standard report exist: S_ALR_87012179 - Customer List, S_ALR_87012180 - Address List, S_ALR_87012182 - Display Changes to Customers. If the reports are not detailed enough then a query or quickview could be created. Implementation of the dual control can help to check sensitive - critical fields.

Queries.Description: FI-MM-SD: Delete Master Data (Vendors-Customers-GL) (non productive Cy Code)
MM-MD: Mass Maintain Material Master Data
Queries.Comment: The maintenance of material master data should be limited to and segregated between Production, Purchasing and Accounting. This can be done on maintenance status (view).
Queries.Risk:
Material Master Data is key Master Data in SAP R/3 as it has links to Sales, Purchasing, Production Planning, Material Forecasting, Distribution and Invoicing. Basically, businesses cannot utilize SAP R/3 without a properly configured Material Master and properly maintained Material Master Data.
E.g. when a material number is entered into a sales order. SAP automatically transfers relative data like item category, delivering plant, cost, and export data directly into the sales order. This eliminated user creation of this data, but also shows the importance of correct material master data.
Several different views of Material Master Data exist in SAP. General/ Basic data view applies to all organizational levels and exists at client (Mandant) level and contains Material Number, Description, Unit of measure, Division, Technical Data, Language, Purchasing data view applies to Plant level and contains Purchasing group, Base unit of measure, MRP Type, Planned delivery time, Batch Indicator, Profit Center, Finance and Controlling view applies to Plant level and contains Price Control, Account Group, Standard Price, Moving Average Price, Pricing Unit Other views refer to Sales Organizations, Storage Locations and Batch information
Some important/relevant Material Master Fields The automatic PO indicator specifies that purchase orders are generated automatically when requisitions are converted The purchasing value key specifies the value key to be used for the default values for various fields for purchase orders raised against the material - including over-delivery tolerances The source list indicator specifies that the source list must have been maintained in the case of external procurement for a certain plant Quality Inspection specifies whether the material is subject to quality inspection, and whether a goods receipt is posted to stock in quality inspection Item Category group Indicator in the sales organization screen triggers the item category in a sales document and the schedule line category Material statistics group key indicator triggers tracking in the Sales Information System Standard, Moving Average & Price Control Fields trigger for all Material Movements whether Standard or Moving Average Price as the unit price times quantity for the movement value will be used Relevant for costing indicator specifies whether the material is subject to automated system generated pricing
Proper control of standard prices is crucial in any system but even more in SAP as all material movements are posted at the standard (std) or moving average price (mva) in the material master. The difference between std and mva is determined by the price control field in the accounting screen of the material master. Many organizations use mva pricing for raw materials as it reflects the average price of all activity for that material. This allows them to use the cost that’s closest to actual for production. Moving average pricing for finished goods could create differences in price between production plants and external shipping points. Any differences in stock transfer between plants could cause unnecessary variances being posted, which are direct differences to the P & L financial statement.
The creation of material master should be restricted to a limited number of users. The integrity of all transactional data and reporting, depends on the quality of the material master data.

Queries.Description: MM: Maintain Vendor Master Data Account group

Queries.Comment: Should be limited to the Purchasing Department and/or Accounts Payable department.
Queries.Risk:
Vendor Master data is stored at three levels: 1. General data applies to every company code and every purchasing organization. The general area includes, for example, the vendor's name, address, language, and telephone number. 2. Company code data that is specific to an individual company code. Company code data includes, for example, reconciliation account number and payment terms. 3. Purchasing organization data specific to purchasing organizations and relevant to raising requests for quotations, purchase orders etc. For example - conditions, minimum order value..
Separate transactions and authorizations are available to segregate maintenance of Company Code (Accounting) and Purchasing data. They can also be maintained centrally using a single transaction.
Each vendor must be assigned to an account group. This then determines the account number assignment and screen layouts.
One-time vendor accounts are used for vendors from whom goods are expected only to be procured once or very rarely. Where one-time vendors are required, a separate account group is normally established in conjunction with a one-time vendor master record. The initial screen for the account group includes a flag to specify that the group is for one-time accounts. Since address and bank account details are entered during invoice/order entry a normal segregation of duties does not operate and compensating controls need to be considered. These might include: - Exception reporting of one-time vendor transactions to facilitate independent review - Use of blocking flags to enforce independent release for payment
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - increased vulnerability to fraud, creation of dummy suppliers customers, … - sub-optimal use or loss of purchasing power

Queries.Description: SD-GEN: Maintain Sales, Shipping & Billing Output

Queries.Risk: These transaction codes and authorizations enable a user to display and modify the table content. Please note that SAP is a table driven application and that all customizing, system settings, application data and master data are stored in tables. Direct table access is the most used backdoor in security. Users that have table maintenance functionality can not only access confidential data but also change and delete it.
Queries.Recommendation:
<NA> variant
* As a first step, consider putting this functionality in a seperate role / profile and assign it more selectively.
* Investigate for what tables the SE16, SE17, SM30 and SM31 tcodes are currently used.
* Implement an alternative for these identified tables: create own parameter transaction codes calling SM30 for the list of specific tables.
* Give the business an appropriate period of time to give the required information, but put a deadline on the fact that the listed transactions will be taken away from business profiles.
ALL variant
* In the affected roles, analyze what tcodes need the S_TABU_DIS object.
* For these tcodes, identify the tables it is using.
* For these table, establish what the authorization groups are.
* Implement these specific authorization groups in these affected profiles.

Queries.Risk: To maintain his/her own spools a user only needs transaction code SP01 without any authorizations on the selected objects. If a user's access needs to be extended to spool administrator functions, he/she needs authorizations for SP01 in S_ADMI_FCD In combination with S_SPO_ACT. When you grant this value, a user has access to all spools, also the spools which contain confidential information.
Queries.Recommendation: * Remove (at least) the DELE, ATTR and AUTH values out of the S_SPO_ACT object where not needed.

Queries.Risk: Direct development changes in a productive system cause untested functionality to be introduced, cause inconsistencies in your system landscape and can jeopardize the integrity and availability of the productive environment. Development access should therefore be restricted to a development environment only.
Queries.Recommendation:
<NA> variant:
* Eliminate all maintenance accesses out of the S_DEVELOP object.
ALL variant:
* If needed at all, at least implement restrictions on development class and object type in the S_DEVELOP object in the mentioned roles.

Queries.Risk: Since most ABAPs do not have authorization groups and own developed ABAPs usually lack authority checks, a backdoor is created by giving users access to transaction codes that start ABAPs directly.
Queries.Recommendation: * Perform the same steps as for the SA38 transaction (S0010SA38A) in order to remove the backdoor transactions from the authorizations.

Queries.Description: ALL_Variant - BC: Remote function call (RFC) access
Queries.Risk: The selected object controls the authorizations to remote function calls to program modules. The authorization needs to be granted in the remote target system. This authorization object will become more and more important in a mySAP environment.
Queries.Recommendation:
* Consider limiting the S_RFC authorizations to only those users who need to connect to the SAP system via an external application.
* Consider implementing restrictions on RFC_NAME to limit the users to the specific purposes they need the S_RFC authorizations for.

Queries.Risk: This authorization provides all functionality on system administration.
Queries.Recommendation: * Consider removing the S_ADMI_FCD authorizations from all functional roles. System administration functionality should only be granted to real system administrators.

Queries.Description: CO: PC-PCP: Maintain Mixed Cost Estimate
SD: I/E: Maintain Foreign Trade Worklist
ALL_Variant - BC: Maintain Batch Input Sessions
Queries.Comment: For processing a batch input session, one needs authorizations to the underlying objects of the processed transaction(s).
Queries.Risk: Batch input sessions can be considered as a mass transaction, making multiple changes to data in one session. The quality and integrity control of the input data often lies outside the SAP system. If erroneous data is processed, the error will be in the SAP system for all records in the session. Also, processing a same BIM twice can lead to duplicate (fictitious) entries. If confidential data is contained in a BIM, then granting to broad access to all BIMs could lead to confidentiality issues.
Queries.Recommendation:
<NA> variant:
* Reduce the number of users having access to BIMs.
ALL variant:
* For the users that really need it, implement adequate session name restrictions.
* Apply a strong naming convention for session names.

Queries.Description: HR: Maintain PA Master Data - Infty 0008 (Payroll)
HR: Display PA Master Data - Infty 0016 (Payroll)
HR: Display PA Master Data - Infty 0021
HR: Display PA Master Data - Infty 0022
HR: All HR Reporting (independent check on infotype and org. assignment) (disregard tcode)
Queries.Comment:
Note that an ABAP authorization for report SAPDBPNP with COARS = 2 means that all HR reports based on the logical databases PNP or PAP (nearly all reports) cannot perform any more authorization checks. In general, you will only want to deactivate the authorization checks for a very small number of Reports. In case of doubt, do not assign your users authorizations for the P_ABAP object.
Furthermore, note that this authorization object differs from the object S_PROGRAM ( ABAP: Program Run Checks ). The latter is used for general program authorization checks. In HR reports, these checks are carried out in addition to the HR infotype authorization check. HR Reporting, however, overrides the HR infotype authorization check for selected reports, with the result that the authorization checks are weakened or completely switched off.
Queries.Risk:
Granting authorizations for directly starting ABAPs via SA38 implies that the S_TCODE authorizations can be circumvented. Because there is a limited number of objects in the HR module, they are 'shared' by a lot of HR functionality. Therefore, the S_TCODE authorizations provide a required additional barriere to have an adequate security in place. Circumventing this barriere significantly weakens the implemented authorization concept.
Moreover, granting full access to the P_ABAP object circumvents the implemented P_ORGIN authorizations, the central object in securing HR data. The P_ABAP object is meant to be granted to users that already have extensive P_ORGIN authorizations to improve the performance of some reports. This improved performance is achieved by not checking the P_ORGIN restrictions !

Queries.Risk:
The payment run is the last stage before payment orders leave the organization. Although SAP provides numerous features, both inherent and configurable, excess access to the payment functionality seriously increases risks for fraud or abusive use of corporate funds.
SAP allows changes to be made to the details held in the proposal run. All changes are only valid within the proposal and do not affect the original documents. Appropriate controls should ensure that changes performed are reasonable and complete. Fields that are changeable include:· Payment (payment method, house bank detail, etc.); and ·Paid items (block indicators, cash discounts, etc.)

ROLE: Definition of GTB-Roles
The key area ROLE is for role maintenance which makes it possible ot limit the access in the Generic Data Browser to certain columns and field content of tables.
To maintain roles the user needs activity '01' and no entry assigned in GTB_NAME.
Enter the name of the role in GTB_NAME and the Activity '03' (Display) in ACTVT to assign a role to a user.

This process give you the access to the maintenance of the general data and the company code data of the vendor master data.
Vendor Master data is stored at three levels: 1. General data applies to every company code and every purchasing organization. The general area includes, for example, the vendor's name, address, language, telephone number, bank account and VAT numbers.. 2. Company code data that is specific to an individual company code. Company code data includes, for example, reconciliation account number and payment terms. 3. Purchasing organization data specific to purchasing organizations and relevant to raising requests for quotations, purchase orders etc. For example - conditions, minimum order value..
Separate transactions and authorizations are available to segregate maintenance of Company Code (Accounting) and Purchasing data. They can also be maintained centrally using a single transaction.
Each vendor must be assigned to an account group. This then determines the account number assignment and screen layouts.
One-time vendor accounts are used for vendors from whom goods are expected only to be procured once or very rarely. Where one-time vendors are required, a separate account group is normally established in conjunction with a one-time vendor master record. The initial screen for the account group includes a flag to specify that the group is for one-time accounts. Since address and bank account details are entered during invoice/order entry a normal segregation of duties does not operate and compensating controls need to be considered. These might include: - Exception reporting of one-time vendor transactions to facilitate independent review - Use of blocking flags to enforce independent release for payment
Queries.Risk: Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like: - increased vulnerability to fraud, creation of dummy suppliers - sub-optimal use or loss of purchasing power
Queries.ControlObjective: Check all new entries in the vendor master data in order to avoid double or triple entries. Some sensitive and critical fields, like Tax information, VAT registration numbers and Bank details should be defined and checked. Changes on sensitive and critical fields should be monitored. Some sensitive and critical fields should be set up as mandatory fields to be filled in.
Queries.SuggestedControls: Display changes to vendor master data: S_ALR_87012089
Queries.Recommendation: Should be limited to the (De) Central master data maintenance Team. The company code views, if no master data maintenance team, should be limited to Accounts Payable department.

Queries.Comment: This process gives you access to the maintenance of customer on general data and company code data. The company code data should be restricted only to specific individuals within the Finance department / or to the master data team if the maintenance is centralized.
Queries.Risk:
General data is accessible to both sales and distribution (SD) and accounting (company code). It consists of customer-specific details, such as the customer’s name, address, and contact information, bank account and VAT registration numbers. The general data is maintained at the client level. Company code data is for financial accounting information. (like reconciliation account, payment terms, payment method,..)
From a financial viewpoint, there are two levels of a customer master record: General data that is entered once for a client (i.e., address, bank details) Company code data (i.e., reconciliation account) can vary for each company code. Examples of company code data are: Payment transactions, Dunning, Correspondence, Interest calculation,...
If a customer is maintained centrally (at the client level), there is a third level containing Sales information. In the Sales and Distribution module, a customer’s sales, billing, and shipping information can be recorded. (see query: VCUSTA - XCUSTA)
Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like:
- negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction - increased vulnerability to fraud, creation of dummy customers, ... - wrong VAT declarations,... - posting on wrong reconciliation account,...
Queries.ControlObjective: You should check all new entries in the customer master data in order to avoid double or triple entries. Some sensitive and critical fields, like Tax information, VAT registration numbers and Bank details should be verified. Some sensitive and critical fields should be set up as mandatory fields to be filled in.
Queries.SuggestedControls: To help you some SAP standard report exist: S_ALR_87012179 - Customer List, S_ALR_87012180 - Address List, S_ALR_87012182 - Display Changes to Customers. If the reports are not detailed enough then a query or quickview could be created. Implementation of the dual control can help to check sensitive - critical fields.
